chapters: These are the words that Moshe spoke to all Yisroel beyond the Yarden, in the wilderness, in the Arava opposite Suf, between Paran and between Tofel and Lavan and Chatzeirot and Di Zahav.
Eleven days from Chorev, by way of Mount Seir, until Kadesh Barnea.
And it was in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first of the month, Moshe spoke to the children of Yisroel, according to all that Havayah commanded him to them.
After he smote Sichon, king of the Emorim, who dwells in Cheshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, who dwells in Ashtarot, in Edrei.
Beyond the Yarden, in the land of Moav, Moshe began to expound this Torah, saying.
Havayah our Elokim spoke to us in Chorev, saying: Enough for you of dwelling at this mountain.

Turn, and journey for yourselves, and come to the highlands of the Emorim and to all its neighbors, in the Arava, in the highlands, and in the plain, and in the south, and on the seashore, the land of the Kena'anim, and the Levanon, until the great river, the river Perat.
See, I have given the land before you. Come, take possession of the land that Havayah swore to your fathers, to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yackov, to give to them and to their seed after them.
And I spoke to you at that time, saying: I cannot bear you alone.
Havayah your Elokim has multiplied you, and behold, you are today as the stars of the heavens in multitude.
Havayah, Elokim of your fathers, shall add to you a thousand times as you are, and He shall bless you as He spoke to you.
How shall I bear alone your troubles, and your burdens, and your quarrels?
Provide for yourselves men, wise and understanding and known to your tribes, and I will set them as heads over you.
And you answered me and said: The thing that you have spoken to do is good.

And I took the heads of your tribes, wise and known men, and I set them as heads over you, leaders of thousands and leaders of hundreds and leaders of fifties and leaders of tens, and officers for your tribes.
And I commanded your judges at that time, saying: Hear between your brothers, and judge righteously between a man and his brother and his stranger.

You shall not recognize a face in judgment; you shall hear the small as well as the great; you shall not fear before any man, for the judgment is Elokim's. And the matter that is too hard for you, you shall bring near to me, and I will hear it.
And I commanded you at that time all the things that you shall do.

And we journeyed from Chorev, and we went through all that great and awesome wilderness that you saw, by way of the highlands of the Emorim, as Havayah our Elokim commanded us, and we came to Kadesh Barnea.
And I said to you: You have come to the highlands of the Emorim, which Havayah our Elokim is giving to us.
See, Havayah your Elokim has given the land before you; go up, take possession, as Havayah, Elokim of your fathers, spoke to you; do not fear, and do not be dismayed.

And you all approached me and said: Let us send men before us, and they shall spy out the land for us, and bring back word to us of the way by which we shall go up, and the cities to which we shall come.
And the thing was good in my eyes, and I took from you twelve men, one man for a tribe.
And they turned and went up to the highlands, and came to the valley of Eshkol, and spied it out.
And they took in their hand from the fruit of the land, and brought it down to us, and brought back word to us, and said: The land that Havayah our Elokim is giving to us is good.
And you did not want to go up, and you rebelled against the mouth of Havayah your Elokim.
And you murmured in your tents, and said: In the hatred of Havayah toward us He brought us out of the land of Mitzrayim, to give us into the hand of the Emorim, to destroy us.
Where are we going up? Our brothers have melted our heart, saying: A greater and taller people than we; great and fortified cities up to the heavens; and we also saw the sons of giants there.
And I said to you: Do not be shattered, and do not fear them.
Havayah your Elokim, who goes before you, He will fight for you, according to all that He did for you in Mitzrayim before your eyes.
And in the wilderness, where you saw that Havayah your Elokim carried you, as a man carries his son, in all the way that you went, until you came to this place.
And in this matter you do not believe in Havayah your Elokim.
Who goes before you on the way, to seek out for you a place to encamp, in fire by night, to show you the way in which you shall go, and in the cloud by day.
And Havayah heard the sound of your words, and He was angered, and He swore, saying.
If any man of these men, this evil generation, shall see the good land that I swore to give to your fathers.
Except Kalev son of Yefuneh, he shall see it, and to him I will give the land that he trod upon, and to his children, because he fulfilled after Havayah.
Also with me Havayah was angered because of you, saying: You too shall not come there.
Yehoshua son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall come there; strengthen him, for he shall cause Yisroel to inherit it.
And your children, whom you said would be for plunder, and your sons, who today do not know good and evil, they shall come there, and to them I will give it, and they shall take possession of it.
And you, turn and journey into the wilderness, by way of the Yam Suf.

And you answered and said to me: We have sinned against Havayah; we will go up and fight, according to all that Havayah our Elokim commanded us. And you girded each man his weapons of war, and you dared to go up to the mountain.
And Havayah said to me: Say to them: Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not in your midst, and you shall not be struck down before your enemies.
And I spoke to you, and you did not listen, and you rebelled against the mouth of Havayah, and you acted willfully and went up to the mountain.
And the Emorim who dwell on that mountain came out toward you, and pursued you as the bees do, and struck you down in Seir until Chormah.
And you returned and wept before Havayah, and Havayah did not listen to your voice, and He did not give ear to you.
And you dwelled in Kadesh many days, according to the days that you dwelled.
And we turned and journeyed into the wilderness, by way of the Yam Suf, as Havayah spoke to me, and we circled Mount Seir many days.
And Havayah said to me, saying.
Enough for you of circling this mountain; turn to the north.
And command the people, saying: You are passing through the border of your brothers, the children of Esav, who dwell in Seir, and they will fear you, and you shall be very careful.
Do not provoke them, for I will not give you of their land even the treading of the sole of a foot, for I have given Mount Seir to Esav as an inheritance.
You shall buy food from them with silver, and eat; and you shall buy water from them with silver, and drink.

For Havayah your Elokim has blessed you in all the work of your hand; He has known your going through this great wilderness; these forty years Havayah your Elokim has been with you; you have not lacked anything.
And we passed from our brothers, the children of Esav, who dwell in Seir, from the way of the Arava, from Eilat and from Etzyon Gever, and we turned and passed by way of the wilderness of Moav.
And Havayah said to me: Do not besiege Moav, and do not provoke war with them, for I will not give you of his land a possession, for to the children of Lot I have given Ar as a possession.
The Eimim dwelled there before, a great and many and tall people, as the giants.
Refaim they also were counted, as the giants, and the Moavim call them Eimim.

And in Seir the Chorim dwelled before, and the children of Esav dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them, and dwelled in their place, as Yisroel did to the land of his possession, which Havayah gave to them.
Now rise and cross the Zered Ravine. And we crossed the Zered Ravine.

And the days that we went from Kadesh Barnea until we crossed the Zered Ravine were thirty-eight years, until all the generation, the men of war, had finished dying from the midst of the camp, as Havayah swore to them.
And also the hand of Havayah was against them, to destroy them from the midst of the camp, until they were finished.
And it was when all the men of war had finished dying from among the people.
And Havayah spoke to me, saying.
You are passing today the border of Moav, Ar.

And you will draw near opposite the children of Ammon; do not besiege them, and do not provoke them, for I will not give you of the land of the children of Ammon a possession, for to the children of Lot I have given it as a possession.
A land of Refaim it also is counted, for Refaim dwelled in it before, and the Ammonim call them Zamzumim.
A great and many and tall people, as the giants, and Havayah destroyed them from before them, and they dispossessed them, and dwelled in their place.
As He did for the children of Esav, who dwell in Seir, when He destroyed the Chorim from before them, and they dispossessed them, and dwelled in their place until this day.
And the Avim, who dwell in villages until Azzah, the Kaftorim, who came out of Kaftor, destroyed them, and dwelled in their place.
Rise, journey, and cross the Arnon Ravine; see, I have given into your hand Sichon, king of Cheshbon the Emori, and his land; begin to take possession, and provoke war with him.
This day I will begin to put terror of you and fear of you upon the peoples under all the heavens, who will hear your report and tremble and be in dread before you.
And I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemot to Sichon, king of Cheshbon, with words of peace, saying.
Let me pass through your land; on the road, on the road I will go; I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
You shall sell me food for silver, and I will eat; and you shall give me water for silver, and I will drink; only let me pass through on foot.
As the children of Esav, who dwell in Seir, did for me, and the Moavim, who dwell in Ar, until I cross the Yarden to the land that Havayah our Elokim is giving to us.
And Sichon, king of Cheshbon, did not want to let us pass through him, for Havayah your Elokim hardened his spirit and strengthened his heart, in order to give him into your hand, as this day.
And Havayah said to me: See, I have begun to give before you Sichon and his land; begin to take possession, to possess his land.
And Sichon came out toward us, he and all his people, to war, to Yahatz.
And Havayah our Elokim gave him before us, and we struck him and his sons and all his people.
And we captured all his cities at that time, and we destroyed every city, men and women and children; we left no remnant.
We plundered only the cattle for ourselves, and the spoil of the cities that we captured.
From Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Ravine, and the city that is in the ravine, until the Gilad, there was no city that was too high for us; all of them Havayah our Elokim gave before us.
Only to the land of the children of Ammon you did not draw near, all the side of the Yabok Ravine, and the cities of the highlands, and all that Havayah our Elokim commanded us.
And we turned and went up by way of the Bashan, and Og, king of the Bashan, came out toward us, he and all his people, to war, at Edrei.
And Havayah said to me: Do not fear him, for into your hand I have given him and all his people and his land, and you shall do to him as you did to Sichon, king of the Emorim, who dwells in Cheshbon.
And Havayah our Elokim gave into our hand also Og, king of Bashan, and all his people, and we smote him until there remained to him no remnant.
And we took all his cities at that time; there was no city that we did not take from them, sixty cities, all the region of Argov, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these were cities fortified, with a high wall, gates and a bar, besides the very many unwalled cities.
And we destroyed them, as we did to Sichon, king of Cheshbon, destroying every city, men and women and children.
And we plundered all the cattle and the spoil of the cities for ourselves.
And we took at that time the land from the hand of the two kings of the Emorim, who are beyond the Yarden, from the Arnon Ravine until Mount Chermon.
The Tzidonim call Chermon Siryon, and the Emorim call it Senir.
All the cities of the plain, and all the Gilad, and all the Bashan, until Salchah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

For only Og, king of Bashan, remained of the remnant of the Refaim; behold, his bed is a bed of iron — is it not in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? Nine cubits its length, and four cubits its width, by the cubit of a man.
And we took possession of this land at that time, from Aroer, which is by the Arnon Ravine, and half of Mount Gilad and its cities, I gave to the Reuvenites and to the Gadites.
And I gave the rest of Gilad, and all the Bashan, the kingdom of Og, to half the tribe of Menasheh, all the region of Argov, for all the Bashan — that is called the land of Refaim.
Yair son of Menasheh took all the region of Argov, until the border of the Geshurim and the Maachatim, and he called them after his name, the Bashan, Chavot Yair, until this day.
And I gave Gilad to Machir.
And I gave to the Reuvenites and to the Gadites from Gilad until the Arnon Ravine, the middle of the ravine and the border, until the Yabok Ravine, the border of the children of Ammon.
And the Arava, and the Yarden, and the border, from the Kinneret until the sea of the Arava, the Salt Sea, below the slopes of the Pisgah eastward.
And I commanded you at that time, saying: Havayah your Elokim has given you this land to possess it; you shall pass over armed before your brothers, the children of Yisroel, all the men of valor.
Only your wives, and your children, and your livestock — I know that you have much livestock — they shall dwell in your cities that I have given you.

Until Havayah gives rest to your brothers as to you, and they too possess the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving them beyond the Yarden; then you shall return each man to his possession that I have given you.
And I commanded Yehoshua at that time, saying: Your eyes have seen all that Havayah your Elokim has done to these two kings; so shall Havayah do to all the kingdoms that you are crossing over to.
You shall not fear them, for Havayah your Elokim, He fights for you.
And I pleaded to Havayah at that time, saying.

My Master Havayah, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your mighty hand; for what god is there in the heavens or on the earth who can do according to Your deeds and according to Your mighty acts?
Let me cross, please, and see the good land that is beyond the Yarden, that good mountain, and the Levanon.
And Havayah was angered with me because of you, and He did not listen to me, and Havayah said to me: Enough for you; do not add to speak to Me further in this matter.
Go up to the top of the Pisgah, and lift your eyes westward and northward and southward and eastward, and see with your eyes, for you shall not cross this Yarden.
And command Yehoshua, and strengthen him and encourage him, for he shall cross before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land that you will see.
And we dwelled in the valley opposite Beit Peor.
And now, Yisroel, hear the statutes and the ordinances that I teach you to do, so that you may live, and come and possess the land that Havayah, Elokim of your fathers, is giving to you.
You shall not add to the word that I command you, and you shall not take away from it, to keep the commandments of Havayah your Elokim that I command you.
Your eyes have seen what Havayah did at Baal Peor, for every man who went after Baal Peor, Havayah your Elokim destroyed him from your midst.
And you who cling to Havayah your Elokim are alive, all of you, today.
See, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, as Havayah my Elokim commanded me, to do so in the midst of the land that you are coming there to possess.

And you shall keep and do them, for it is your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples, who shall hear all these statutes and say: Only a wise and understanding people is this great nation.
For what great nation is there that has Elokim near to it, as Havayah our Elokim is to us in all our calling to Him?
And what great nation is there that has statutes and ordinances righteous, as all this Torah that I place before you today?

Only beware for yourself, and guard your soul greatly, lest you forget the things that your eyes saw, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life, and you shall make them known to your children and to your children's children.

The day that you stood before Havayah your Elokim at Chorev, when Havayah said to me: Gather the people to Me, and I will let them hear My words, that they may learn to fear Me all the days that they live upon the earth, and their children they shall teach.
And you approached and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire to the heart of the heavens, darkness, cloud, and thick fog.
And Havayah spoke to you from the midst of the fire; you were hearing a sound of words, but you were not seeing an image, only a sound.
And He told you His covenant that He commanded you to do, the Ten Words, and He wrote them upon two tablets of stone.
And Havayah commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, to do them in the land that you are crossing over there to possess.
And you shall guard your souls greatly, for you did not see any image on the day Havayah spoke to you at Chorev, from the midst of the fire.
Lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image, the likeness of any shape, the form of a male or the form of a female.
The form of any beast that is on the earth, the form of any winged bird that flies in the heavens.
The form of anything that creeps on the ground, the form of any fish that is in the water under the earth.

And lest you lift your eyes to the heavens, and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of the heavens, and you be drawn astray and bow to them and serve them, which Havayah your Elokim apportioned to all the peoples under all the heavens.
And you, Havayah took you, and brought you out of the iron furnace, from Mitzrayim, to be for Him a people of inheritance, as this day.
And Havayah was angered with me because of you, and He swore that I would not cross the Yarden, and that I would not come to the good land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you as an inheritance.
For I will die in this land; I am not crossing the Yarden, and you are crossing, and you shall possess that good land.

Beware for yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of Havayah your Elokim, which He made with you, and make for yourselves a carved image, the likeness of anything that Havayah your Elokim commanded you.
For Havayah your Elokim is a consuming fire, a zealous El.

When you beget children and children's children, and you have been long in the land, and you act corruptly and make a carved image, the likeness of anything, and do evil in the eyes of Havayah your Elokim, to anger Him.

I call to witness against you today the heavens and the earth, that you shall surely perish quickly from the land that you are crossing the Yarden there to possess it; you shall not prolong your days upon it, for you shall be destroyed.
And Havayah will scatter you among the peoples, and you shall remain few in number among the nations where Havayah will lead you.
And you shall serve there gods, the work of the hands of man, wood and stone, which do not see and do not hear and do not eat and do not smell.
And you shall seek from there Havayah your Elokim, and you shall find Him, when you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul.
When you are in distress, and all these things have found you, in the end of days, you shall return to Havayah your Elokim, and you shall listen to His voice.
For Havayah your Elokim is a merciful El; He will not abandon you, and He will not destroy you, and He will not forget the covenant of your fathers that He swore to them.

For ask now of the first days that were before you, from the day that Elokim created man upon the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens, has there been like this great thing, or has there been heard like it?
Has a people heard the voice of Elokim speaking from the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and lived?

Or has a god tried to come to take for himself a nation from the midst of a nation, with trials, with signs, and with wonders, and with war, and with a mighty hand, and with an outstretched arm, and with great terrors, according to all that Havayah your Elokim did for you in Mitzrayim before your eyes?
You have been shown to know that Havayah, He is Elokim; there is none besides Him.
From the heavens He let you hear His voice to discipline you, and on earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words from the midst of the fire.
And because He loved your fathers, and chose his seed after him, and He brought you out before Him with His great power from Mitzrayim.
To drive out nations greater and mightier than you from before you, to bring you, to give you their land as an inheritance, as this day.
And you shall know today, and return it to your heart, that Havayah, He is Elokim, in the heavens above and on the earth below; there is none other.

And you shall keep His statutes and His commandments that I command you today, that it may be good for you and for your children after you, and that you may prolong your days upon the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you, all the days.
Then Moshe separated three cities beyond the Yarden, toward the rising of the sun.
For a killer to flee there, who kills his neighbor without knowledge, and he did not hate him from yesterday or the day before.
Betzer in the wilderness, in the land of the plain, for the Reuvenites; and Ramot in Gilad for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Menashites.
And this is the Torah that Moshe placed before the children of Yisroel.
These are the testimonies and the statutes and the ordinances that Moshe spoke to the children of Yisroel, in their coming out of Mitzrayim.
Beyond the Yarden, in the valley opposite Beit Peor, in the land of Sichon, king of the Emorim, who dwelled in Cheshbon, whom Moshe and the children of Yisroel smote in their coming out of Mitzrayim.
And they took possession of his land, and the land of Og, king of Bashan, the two kings of the Emorim, who are beyond the Yarden, toward the rising of the sun.
From Aroer, which is on the bank of the Arnon Ravine, until Mount Tziyon, which is Chermon.
And all the Arava beyond the Yarden eastward, until the sea of the Arava, below the slopes of the Pisgah.
And Moshe called all Yisroel, and said to them: Hear, Yisroel, the statutes and the ordinances that I speak in your ears today, and learn them, and take care to do them.
Havayah our Elokim made a covenant with us at Chorev.
Not with our fathers did Havayah make this covenant, but with us, we, these here, all of us alive today.
Face to face Havayah spoke with you at the mountain, from the midst of the fire.
I was standing between Havayah and you at that time, to tell you the word of Havayah, for you were afraid because of the fire, and you did not go up the mountain, saying.
I am Havayah your Elokim, who brought you out of the land of Mitzrayim, from the house of bondage.
You shall have no other gods before Me.
You shall not make for yourself a carved image, any likeness of that which is in the heavens above, or that which is on the earth below, or that which is in the waters beneath the earth.

You shall not bow to them, and you shall not serve them, for I am Havayah your Elokim, a zealous El, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the third and upon the fourth generation, of those who hate Me.
And doing kindness to thousands, to those who love Me and keep My commandments.
You shall not take the name of Havayah your Elokim in vain, for Havayah will not clear one who takes His name in vain.
Observe the Shabbos day, to keep it holy, as Havayah your Elokim commanded you.
Six days you shall labor, and do all your work.

And the seventh day is a Shabbos to Havayah your Elokim; you shall not do any work, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your slave, and your maidservant, and your ox, and your donkey, and all your animals, and your stranger who is within your gates, so that your slave and your maidservant may rest as you do.

And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Mitzrayim, and Havayah your Elokim brought you out from there with a mighty hand and with an outstretched arm; therefore Havayah your Elokim commanded you to keep the Shabbos day.
Honor your father and your mother, as Havayah your Elokim commanded you, so that your days may be prolonged, and so that it may be good for you.
You shall not murder; and you shall not commit adultery; and you shall not steal; and you shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
And you shall not covet your neighbor's wife, and you shall not desire your neighbor's house, his field, or his slave, or his maidservant, his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor's.

Havayah spoke these words to all your assembly at the mountain, from the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the fog, a great voice, and it did not cease; and He wrote them on two tablets of stone, and gave them to me.
And it was when you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness, and the mountain was burning with fire, that you approached me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders.
And you said: Behold, Havayah our Elokim has shown us His glory and His greatness, and we heard His voice from the midst of the fire; this day we have seen that Elokim speaks with man, and he lives.
And now, why should we die, for this great fire will consume us; if we continue to hear the voice of Havayah our Elokim further, we shall die.
For who is there of all flesh who heard the voice of the living Elokim speaking from the midst of the fire, as we have, and lived?
Approach you, and hear all that Havayah our Elokim will say, and you shall speak to us all that Havayah our Elokim speaks to you, and we will hear and do.

And Havayah heard the sound of your words, in your speaking to me, and Havayah said to me: I have heard the sound of the words of this people that they spoke to you; they have done well in all that they spoke.
Would that this heart were theirs, to fear Me and to keep all My commandments all the days, so that it would be good for them and for their children forever.
Go, say to them: Return to your tents.

And you, stand here with Me, and I will speak to you all the commandment, and the statutes, and the ordinances, that you shall teach them, and they shall do them in the land that I am giving them to possess.
And you shall take care to do as Havayah your Elokim commanded you; you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left.
In all the way that Havayah your Elokim commanded you, you shall walk, so that you may live, and it may be good for you, and you may prolong your days in the land that you shall possess.
And this is the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances, that Havayah your Elokim commanded to teach you, to do them in the land that you are crossing over there to possess.

So that you will fear Havayah your Elokim, to keep all His statutes and His commandments that I command you, you and your son and your son's son, all the days of your life, and so that your days may be prolonged.

And you shall hear, Yisroel, and take care to do it, so that it will be good for you, and so that you will increase greatly, as Havayah, Elokim of your fathers, spoke to you, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Hear, Yisroel: Havayah our Elokim, Havayah is one.
And you shall love Havayah your Elokim with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.
And these words that I command you today shall be upon your heart.
And you shall teach them diligently to your children, and speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk on the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise.
And you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand, and they shall be as ornaments between your eyes.
And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your house, and upon your gates.
And it shall be when Havayah your Elokim brings you to the land that He swore to your fathers, to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yackov, to give to you, great and good cities that you did not build.
And houses full of all good that you did not fill, and cisterns hewn that you did not hew, vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant, and you shall eat and be satisfied.
Beware, lest you forget Havayah, who brought you out of the land of Mitzrayim, from the house of bondage.
You shall fear Havayah your Elokim, and you shall serve Him, and by His name you shall swear.
You shall not go after other gods, from the gods of the peoples that are around you.
For Havayah your Elokim is a zealous El in your midst, lest the anger of Havayah your Elokim burn against you.
You shall not test Havayah your Elokim, as you tested Him at Massah.
You shall keep the commandments of Havayah your Elokim, and His testimonies, and His statutes, that He commanded you.
And you shall do the right and the good in the eyes of Havayah, so that it will be good for you, and you will come and possess the good land that Havayah swore to your fathers.
To drive out all your enemies from before you, as Havayah spoke.
When your son asks you tomorrow, saying: What are the testimonies, and the statutes, and the ordinances, that Havayah our Elokim commanded you?
And you shall say to your son: We were slaves to Paroh in Mitzrayim, and Havayah brought us out of Mitzrayim with a mighty hand.
And Havayah gave signs and wonders, great and terrible, upon Mitzrayim, upon Paroh, and upon all his household, before our eyes.
And He brought us out from there, in order to bring us, to give us the land that He swore to our fathers.
And Havayah commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear Havayah our Elokim, for our good all the days, to keep us alive, as this day.
And righteousness shall be ours, if we take care to do all this commandment before Havayah our Elokim, as He commanded us.

When Havayah your Elokim brings you to the land that you are coming there to possess it, and He casts out many nations from before you, the Chiti and the Girgashi and the Emori and the Kena'ani and the Perizi and the Chivi and the Yevusi, seven nations greater and mightier than you.
And Havayah your Elokim gives them before you, and you smite them; you shall utterly destroy them; you shall not make a covenant with them, and you shall not show them favor.
And you shall not marry them; you shall not give your daughter to his son, and you shall not take his daughter for your son.
For he will turn your son from after Me, and they will serve other gods, and the anger of Havayah will burn against you, and He will destroy you quickly.
But so shall you do to them: you shall tear down their altars, and shatter their standing stones, and cut down their sacred trees, and burn their carved images in fire.
For you are a holy people to Havayah your Elokim; Havayah your Elokim has chosen you to be for Him a treasured people.
Not because you are more than all the peoples did Havayah desire you and choose you, for you are the fewest of all the peoples.

But because of the love of Havayah for you, and because He keeps the oath that He swore to your fathers, Havayah brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeemed you from the house of bondage, from the hand of Paroh, king of Mitzrayim.
And you shall know that Havayah your Elokim, He is Elokim, the faithful El, keeping the covenant and the kindness for those who love Him and keep His commandments, for a thousand generations.
And repaying His enemies to his face, to destroy him; He will not delay for His enemy, to his face He will repay him.
And you shall keep the commandment, and the statutes, and the ordinances, that I command you today, to do them.
And it shall be, because you listen to these ordinances, and keep them and do them, Havayah your Elokim will keep for you the covenant and the kindness that He swore to your fathers.

And He will love you, and bless you, and multiply you, and bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land, your grain and your wine and your oil, the increase of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep, in the land that He swore to your fathers to give to you.
Blessed shall you be above all the peoples; there shall not be among you a barren male or a barren female, or among your cattle.
And Havayah will remove from you all sickness, and He will not put upon you all the evil diseases of Mitzrayim that you knew, but He will put them upon all your enemies.
And you shall consume all the peoples that Havayah your Elokim gives to you; your eye shall not pity them, and you shall not serve their gods, for it is a snare for you.
If you say in your heart: These nations are more numerous than I; how can I dispossess them?
You shall not fear them; remember what Havayah your Elokim did to Paroh, and to all Mitzrayim.

The great trials that your eyes saw, and the signs, and the wonders, and the mighty hand, and the outstretched arm, with which Havayah your Elokim brought you out; so shall Havayah your Elokim do to all the peoples that you fear.
And Havayah your Elokim will also send the hornet among them, until those who remain and those who hide from before you are destroyed.
You shall not be broken before them, for Havayah your Elokim is in your midst, a great and awesome El.
And Havayah your Elokim will cast out those nations from before you little by little; you will not be able to finish them quickly, lest the beasts of the field multiply against you.
And Havayah your Elokim will give them before you, and confound them with great confusion, until they are destroyed.
And He will give their kings into your hand, and you shall wipe out their name from under the heavens; no man shall stand before you, until you destroy them.

You shall burn the carved images of their gods in fire; you shall not covet the silver and the gold that are upon them, and take it for yourself, lest you be ensnared by it, for it is an abomination to Havayah your Elokim.
And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, and you shall become banned like it; you shall utterly detest it, and you shall utterly abhor it, for it is banned.
You shall take care to do all the commandment that I command you today, so that you may live and multiply, and come and possess the land that Havayah swore to your fathers.

And you shall remember all the way that Havayah your Elokim led you these forty years in the wilderness, to humble you, to test you, to know what is in your heart, whether you will keep His commandments or not.

And He humbled you, and let you hunger, and fed you the manna, which you did not know, and your fathers did not know, in order to make you know that not by bread alone does man live, but by all that comes from the mouth of Havayah does man live.
Your garment did not wear out upon you, and your foot did not swell, these forty years.
And you shall know in your heart, that as a man chastises his son, so Havayah your Elokim chastises you.
And you shall keep the commandments of Havayah your Elokim, to walk in His ways, and to fear Him.
For Havayah your Elokim is bringing you to a good land, a land of streams of water, springs and depths, coming out in the valley and on the mountain.
A land of wheat and barley, and vines and figs and pomegranates, a land of oil-olives and honey.
A land in which you shall eat bread without poverty; you shall not lack anything in it; a land whose stones are iron, and from whose hills you shall dig copper.
And you shall eat and be satisfied, and bless Havayah your Elokim for the good land that He gave you.
Beware, lest you forget Havayah your Elokim, to not keep His commandments and His ordinances and His statutes that I command you today.
Lest you eat and be satisfied, and build good houses, and dwell in them.
And your cattle and your flocks multiply, and silver and gold multiply for you, and all that is yours multiplies.
And your heart is lifted up, and you forget Havayah your Elokim, who brought you out of the land of Mitzrayim, from the house of bondage.
Who led you in the great and awesome wilderness, fiery serpents and scorpions and thirst where there is no water, who brought out water for you from the rock of flint.
Who fed you manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know, to humble you, and to test you, to do good for you in your end.
And you will say in your heart: My power and the might of my hand made me this wealth.
And you shall remember Havayah your Elokim, for He is the One who gives you power to make wealth, to establish His covenant that He swore to your fathers, as this day.
And it shall be, if you forget Havayah your Elokim, and go after other gods, and serve them and bow to them, I warn you today that you shall surely perish.
Like the nations that Havayah destroys from before you, so shall you perish, because you did not listen to the voice of Havayah your Elokim.
Hear, Yisroel: you are crossing the Yarden today, to come to dispossess greater and mightier nations than you, great and fortified cities up to the heavens.
A great and tall people, sons of giants, whom you knew, and you heard: Who can stand before the sons of giants?

And you shall know today that Havayah your Elokim, He is the One who passes before you, a consuming fire; He will destroy them, and He will bring them down before you, and you shall dispossess them and destroy them quickly, as Havayah spoke to you.

Do not say in your heart, when Havayah your Elokim casts them out from before you, saying: Because of my righteousness Havayah brought me to possess this land; and because of the wickedness of these nations Havayah dispossesses them from before you.

Not because of your righteousness, and not because of the uprightness of your heart, are you coming to possess their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations Havayah your Elokim dispossesses them from before you, and in order to establish the word that Havayah swore to your fathers, to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yackov.
And you shall know that not because of your righteousness is Havayah your Elokim giving you this good land to possess it, for you are a stiff-necked people.

Remember, do not forget, how you angered Havayah your Elokim in the wilderness; from the day that you came out of the land of Mitzrayim, until you came to this place, you have been defiant against Havayah.
And at Chorev you angered Havayah, and Havayah was angered with you, to destroy you.

In my going up to the mountain to take the tablets of stone, the Tablets of the Covenant that Havayah made with you, and I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I did not eat bread, and I did not drink water.

And Havayah gave me the two tablets of stone, written with the finger of Elokim, and upon them were according to all the words that Havayah spoke with you on the mountain, from the midst of the fire, on the day of the assembly.
And it was at the end of forty days and forty nights, Havayah gave me the two tablets of stone, the Tablets of the Covenant.

And Havayah said to me: Rise, go down quickly from here, for your people, whom you brought out of Mitzrayim, have acted corruptly; they have turned quickly from the way that I commanded them; they have made for themselves a cast image.
And Havayah said to me, saying: I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people.
Let Me be, and I will destroy them, and wipe out their name from under the heavens, and I will make you into a nation mightier and more numerous than they.
And I turned and came down from the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire, and the two Tablets of the Covenant were in my two hands.
And I saw, and behold, you had sinned against Havayah your Elokim; you made for yourselves a cast calf; you turned quickly from the way that Havayah commanded you.
And I grasped the two tablets, and cast them from my two hands, and shattered them before your eyes.

And I fell before Havayah, as at the first, forty days and forty nights; I did not eat bread, and I did not drink water, for all your sin that you sinned, to do evil in the eyes of Havayah, to anger Him.
For I was afraid of the anger and the fury with which Havayah was enraged against you, to destroy you; and Havayah listened to me also that time.
And with Aharon Havayah was greatly angered, to destroy him; and I prayed also for Aharon at that time.
And I took your sin that you made, the calf, and burned it in fire, and ground it, grinding well, until it was fine dust, and I threw its dust into the stream that descends from the mountain.
And at Tav'erah, and at Massah, and at Kivrot HaTa'avah, you angered Havayah.

And when Havayah sent you from Kadesh Barnea, saying: Go up and possess the land that I have given you, and you defied the mouth of Havayah your Elokim, and you did not believe in Him, and you did not listen to His voice.
You have been defiant against Havayah from the day I knew you.
And I fell before Havayah the forty days and the forty nights that I fell, for Havayah had said to destroy you.
And I prayed to Havayah, and said: My Master Havayah, do not destroy Your people and Your inheritance, that You redeemed in Your greatness, that You brought out of Mitzrayim with a mighty hand.
Remember Your servants, Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yackov; do not turn to the stubbornness of this people, and to its wickedness, and to its sin.

Lest the people of the land from which You brought us out say: Because of the inability of Havayah to bring them to the land that He spoke to them, and because of His hatred of them, He brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.
And they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out with Your great power and with Your outstretched arm.
At that time Havayah said to me: Carve for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and come up to Me to the mountain, and make for yourself an ark of wood.
And I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets that you shattered, and you shall place them in the ark.
And I made an ark of acacia wood, and carved two tablets of stone like the first, and went up to the mountain, and the two tablets were in my hand.
And He wrote on the tablets, as the first writing, the Ten Words that Havayah spoke to you on the mountain, from the midst of the fire, on the day of the assembly, and Havayah gave them to me.
And I turned and came down from the mountain, and placed the tablets in the ark that I had made, and they were there, as Havayah commanded me.
And the children of Yisroel journeyed from Be'erot Benei Yaakan to Moseirah; there Aharon died, and he was buried there, and Elazar his son served as priest in his place.
From there they journeyed to Gudgod, and from Gudgod to Yotvatah, a land of streams of water.
At that time Havayah separated the tribe of Levi, to carry the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah, to stand before Havayah to serve Him, and to bless in His name, until this day.
Therefore Levi has no portion and no inheritance with his brothers; Havayah is his inheritance, as Havayah your Elokim spoke to him.
And I stayed on the mountain, as the first days, forty days and forty nights, and Havayah listened to me also that time; Havayah did not wish to destroy you.
And Havayah said to me: Rise, go on the journey before the people, and they shall come and possess the land that I swore to their fathers to give to them.

And now, Yisroel, what does Havayah your Elokim ask of you, but to fear Havayah your Elokim, to walk in all His ways, and to love Him, and to serve Havayah your Elokim with all your heart and with all your soul.
To keep the commandments of Havayah, and His statutes that I command you today, for your good.
Behold, the heavens belong to Havayah your Elokim, and the heavens of heavens, the earth and all that is in it.
Havayah desired only your fathers, to love them, and He chose their seed after them, you, from all the peoples, as this day.
And you shall circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and you shall not stiffen your neck anymore.
For Havayah your Elokim, He is Elokim of elokim, and Master of masters, the great El, the mighty, and the awesome, who does not show favor, and does not take a bribe.
Who does judgment for the orphan and the widow, and loves the stranger, to give him food and clothing.
And you shall love the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Mitzrayim.
You shall fear Havayah your Elokim, you shall serve Him, and to Him you shall cleave, and by His name you shall swear.
He is your praise, and He is your Elokim, who did for you these great and awesome things that your eyes saw.
With seventy souls your fathers went down to Mitzrayim, and now Havayah your Elokim has made you as the stars of the heavens for multitude.
And you shall love Havayah your Elokim, and keep His charge, and His statutes, and His ordinances, and His commandments, all the days.
And you shall know today, for not with your children, who did not know and who did not see the discipline of Havayah your Elokim, His greatness, His mighty hand, and His outstretched arm.
And His signs, and His deeds, that He did in the midst of Mitzrayim, to Paroh king of Mitzrayim, and to all his land.
And what He did to the army of Mitzrayim, to its horses and to its chariots, that He flooded the waters of the Yam Suf over them, in their pursuing you, and Havayah destroyed them until this day.
And what He did for you in the wilderness, until you came to this place.

And what He did to Datan and Aviram, sons of Eliav son of Reuven, when the earth opened its mouth, and swallowed them and their households and their tents, and all the substance that was at their feet, in the midst of all Yisroel.
For your eyes are the ones that saw all the great work of Havayah that He did.
And you shall keep all the commandment that I command you today, so that you may be strong, and come and possess the land that you are crossing over there to possess.
And so that you may prolong your days upon the land that Havayah swore to your fathers, to give to them and to their seed, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land that you are coming there to possess is not like the land of Mitzrayim, from which you came out, where you sowed your seed and watered it with your foot, like a vegetable garden.
But the land that you are crossing over there to possess is a land of mountains and valleys; from the rain of the heavens it drinks water.
A land that Havayah your Elokim seeks; always the eyes of Havayah your Elokim are upon it, from the beginning of the year until the end of the year.
And it shall be, if you listen to My commandments that I command you today, to love Havayah your Elokim, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul.
I will give the rain of your land in its time, the early rain and the late rain, and you shall gather your grain, and your wine, and your oil.
And I will give grass in your field for your cattle, and you shall eat and be satisfied.
Beware, lest your heart be seduced, and you turn aside, and serve other gods, and bow to them.

And the anger of Havayah will burn against you, and He will shut the heavens, and there will be no rain, and the ground will not give its produce, and you will quickly perish from the good land that Havayah is giving you.
And you shall place these words of Mine upon your heart and upon your soul, and bind them as a sign upon your hand, and they shall be as ornaments between your eyes.
And you shall teach them to your children, to speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk on the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise.
And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your house, and upon your gates.
So that your days may be many, and the days of your children, upon the land that Havayah swore to your fathers to give them, as the days of the heavens above the earth.
For if you keep all this commandment that I command you, to do it, to love Havayah your Elokim, to walk in all His ways, and to cleave to Him.
Then Havayah will drive out all these nations from before you, and you shall possess greater and mightier nations than you.
Every place that the sole of your foot treads upon shall be yours; from the wilderness and the Levanon, from the river, the Perat River, until the western sea shall be your border.
No man shall stand before you; Havayah your Elokim will put the terror of you and the fear of you upon all the land that you tread upon, as He spoke to you.
See, I place before you today a blessing and a curse.
The blessing, if you listen to the commandments of Havayah your Elokim, that I command you today.
And the curse, if you do not listen to the commandments of Havayah your Elokim, and turn aside from the way that I command you today, to go after other gods that you did not know.
And it shall be, when Havayah your Elokim brings you to the land that you are coming there to possess, you shall give the blessing upon Mount Gerizim, and the curse upon Mount Eival.
Are they not beyond the Yarden, beyond the way of the setting of the sun, in the land of the Kena'ani who dwells in the Arava, opposite Gilgal, beside the plains of Moreh?
For you are crossing the Yarden, to come to possess the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you, and you shall possess it, and dwell in it.
And you shall take care to do all the statutes and the ordinances that I place before you today.
These are the statutes and the ordinances that you shall take care to do in the land that Havayah, Elokim of your fathers, has given you to possess it, all the days that you live upon the earth.
You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations that you are dispossessing served their gods, upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every leafy tree.
And you shall tear down their altars, and shatter their standing stones, and burn their sacred trees in fire, and cut down the carved images of their gods, and destroy their name from that place.
You shall not do so to Havayah your Elokim.
But to the place that Havayah your Elokim will choose from all your tribes, to place His name there, you shall seek His dwelling, and you shall come there.

And you shall bring there your burnt offerings, and your peace offerings, and your tithes, and the gift of your hand, and your vows, and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your cattle and of your flocks.
And you shall eat there before Havayah your Elokim, and you shall rejoice in all the sending forth of your hand, you and your households, with which Havayah your Elokim has blessed you.
You shall not do according to all that we are doing here today, each man all that is right in his eyes.
For you have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance that Havayah your Elokim is giving you.

And you shall cross the Yarden, and dwell in the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you as an inheritance, and He will give you rest from all your enemies around you, and you shall dwell in safety.

And it shall be, the place that Havayah your Elokim will choose to rest His name there, there you shall bring all that I command you: your burnt offerings, and your peace offerings, your tithes, and the gift of your hand, and all your choice vows that you vow to Havayah.

And you shall rejoice before Havayah your Elokim, you, and your sons, and your daughters, and your slaves, and your maidservants, and the Levi who is within your gates, for he has no portion and inheritance with you.
Beware, lest you offer up your burnt offerings in any place that you see.
But in the place that Havayah will choose in one of your tribes, there you shall offer up your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I command you.

Only, with all the desire of your soul, you may slaughter and eat meat, according to the blessing of Havayah your Elokim that He gave you, within all your gates; the impure and the pure may eat it, as the gazelle and as the deer.
Only the blood you shall not eat; upon the earth you shall pour it like water.

You may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain and your wine and your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and of your flocks, and all your vows that you vow, and your freewill offerings, and the gift of your hand.

But before Havayah your Elokim you shall eat it, in the place that Havayah your Elokim will choose, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your slave, and your maidservant, and the Levi who is within your gates, and you shall rejoice before Havayah your Elokim in all the sending forth of your hand.
Beware, lest you forsake the Levi, all your days upon your land.
When Havayah your Elokim enlarges your border, as He spoke to you, and you say: I will eat meat, because your soul desires to eat meat, with all the desire of your soul you may eat meat.

If the place that Havayah your Elokim will choose to place His name there is far from you, you shall slaughter from your cattle and from your flock that Havayah gave you, as I commanded you, and you shall eat within your gates, with all the desire of your soul.
Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you shall eat it; the impure and the pure shall eat it.
Only be strong not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life, and you shall not eat the life with the flesh.
You shall not eat it; upon the earth you shall pour it like water.
You shall not eat it, so that it will be good for you and for your children after you, when you do the right in the eyes of Havayah.
You shall take only your holy things that you have, and your vows, and come to the place that Havayah will choose.

And you shall make your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood, upon the altar of Havayah your Elokim; and the blood of your peace offerings shall be poured upon the altar of Havayah your Elokim, and you shall eat the flesh.

Observe and listen to all these words that I command you, so that it will be good for you and for your children after you forever, when you do the good and the right in the eyes of Havayah your Elokim.
When Havayah your Elokim cuts off the nations that you are coming there to dispossess them from before you, and you dispossess them, and dwell in their land.
Beware, lest you be ensnared after them, after they are destroyed from before you, and lest you seek their gods, saying: How did these nations serve their gods, and I too will do so.
You shall not do so to Havayah your Elokim, for every abomination of Havayah that He hates they did for their gods, for even their sons and their daughters they burn in fire for their gods.
You shall take care to do all the matter that I command you; you shall not add to it, and you shall not take away from it.
If a prophet rises in your midst, or a dreamer of a dream, and he gives you a sign or a wonder.
And the sign or the wonder comes, that he spoke to you, saying: Let us go after other gods that you did not know, and serve them.

You shall not listen to the words of that prophet, or to that dreamer of a dream, for Havayah your Elokim is testing you, to know whether you love Havayah your Elokim with all your heart and with all your soul.
You shall walk after Havayah your Elokim, and you shall fear Him, and keep His commandments, and listen to His voice, and serve Him, and cleave to Him.

And that prophet, or that dreamer of a dream, shall be put to death, because he spoke falsehood against Havayah your Elokim, who brought you out of the land of Mitzrayim and redeemed you from the house of bondage, to lead you astray from the path that Havayah your Elokim commanded you to walk in, and you shall remove the evil from your midst.

If your brother, the son of your mother, entices you, or your son, or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your friend who is as your soul, in secret, saying: Let us go and serve other gods that you did not know, you and your fathers.
From the gods of the peoples that are around you, the near to you or the far from you, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth.
You shall not agree with him, and you shall not listen to him, and your eye shall not pity him, and you shall not have compassion, and you shall not cover for him.
But you shall surely kill him; your hand shall be against him first, to put him to death, and the hand of all the people afterward.
And you shall stone him with stones, and he shall die, for he sought to lead you astray from Havayah your Elokim, who brought you out of the land of Mitzrayim, from the house of bondage.
And all Yisroel shall hear and fear, and shall not do again like this evil thing in your midst.
If you hear in one of your cities that Havayah your Elokim is giving you to dwell there, saying.
Lawless men have gone out from your midst, and led astray the inhabitants of their city, saying: Let us go and serve other gods that you did not know.
And you shall inquire, and search, and ask thoroughly, and behold, if it is true, the matter is certain, this abomination was done in your midst.
You shall surely strike the inhabitants of that city by the sword; destroy it, and all that is in it, and its cattle, by the sword.

And all its spoil you shall gather into the midst of its square, and burn in fire the city and all its spoil, entirely, to Havayah your Elokim, and it shall be an everlasting mound; it shall not be built again.

And there shall not cling to your hand anything of the banned property, so that Havayah will turn from the fierceness of His anger, and give you mercy, and have mercy on you, and multiply you, as He swore to your fathers.
When you listen to the voice of Havayah your Elokim, to keep all His commandments that I command you today, to do the right in the eyes of Havayah your Elokim.
You are children of Havayah your Elokim; you shall not cut yourselves, and you shall not make a baldness between your eyes for the dead.
For you are a holy people to Havayah your Elokim, and Havayah chose you to be for Him a treasured people, from all the peoples that are on the face of the earth.
You shall not eat any abomination.
These are the animals that you may eat: ox, sheep, and goat.
Deer, and gazelle, and fallow deer, and wild goat, and oryx, and aurochs, and mouflon.
And every animal that has a hoof, and splits the hoof into two hooves, bringing up the cud, among the animals, you may eat it.

But these you shall not eat, of those that bring up the cud, and of those that have a split hoof: the camel, and the hare, and the hyrax, for they bring up the cud, but they do not split the hoof; they are impure for you.
And the pig, for it has a split hoof, but does not bring up the cud, it is impure for you; of their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall not touch.
This you may eat of all that is in the water: all that has fins and scales you may eat.
And all that does not have fins and scales you shall not eat; it is impure for you.
Every pure bird you may eat.
And this is what you shall not eat of them: the griffon vulture, and the bearded vulture, and the lappet-faced vulture.
And the glede, and the buzzard, and the kite, after its kinds.
And every raven after its kinds.
And the ostrich, and the swift, and the seagull, and the sparrow hawk after its kinds.
The little owl, and the short-eared owl, and the barn owl.
And the eagle owl, and the roller, and the fish owl.
And the stork, and the heron after its kinds, and the hoopoe, and the bat.
And every flying swarming creature is impure for you; they shall not be eaten.
Every pure flying creature you may eat.

You shall not eat any carcass; to the stranger who is within your gates you may give it, and he shall eat it, or sell it to a foreigner, for you are a holy people to Havayah your Elokim. You shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk.
You shall surely tithe all the yield of your sowing, that comes out of the field year by year.

And you shall eat before Havayah your Elokim, in the place that He will choose to rest His name there, the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and your flocks, so that you may learn to fear Havayah your Elokim all the days.

And if the way is too long for you, for you are unable to carry it, because the place that Havayah your Elokim will choose to place His name there is far from you, when Havayah your Elokim blesses you.
And you shall give it for silver, and bind the silver in your hand, and go to the place that Havayah your Elokim will choose.

And you shall spend the silver for whatever your soul desires, for cattle, and for sheep, and for wine, and for strong drink, and for whatever your soul asks, and you shall eat there before Havayah your Elokim, and rejoice, you and your household.
And you shall not forsake the Levi who is within your gates, for he has no portion and inheritance with you.
At the end of three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your yield in that year, and lay it up within your gates.

And the Levi shall come, for he has no portion and inheritance with you, and the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow, who are within your gates, and they shall eat and be satisfied, so that Havayah your Elokim will bless you in all the work of your hand that you do.
At the end of seven years you shall make a release.
And this is the matter of the release: every creditor who lends to his neighbor shall release; he shall not press his neighbor and his brother, for a release has been proclaimed for Havayah.
From the foreigner you may exact it, but your hand shall release that which is yours with your brother.
Only that there shall be no poor among you, for Havayah will surely bless you in the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you as an inheritance, to possess it.
If only you listen to the voice of Havayah your Elokim, to take care to do all this commandment that I command you today.
For Havayah your Elokim has blessed you, as He spoke to you, and you shall lend to many nations, and you shall not borrow.

If there is among you a poor man, one of your brothers, within one of your gates, in your land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you, you shall not harden your heart, and you shall not shut your hand from your poor brother.
But you shall surely open your hand to him, and lend him enough for his need, whatever he lacks.

Beware, lest there be a base word in your heart, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, is near, and your eye is evil toward your poor brother, and you do not give him, and he cries to Havayah against you, and it is a sin in you.

You shall surely give him, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give to him, for because of this thing Havayah your Elokim will bless you in all your work, and in all the sending forth of your hand.
For the poor shall not cease from the midst of the land; therefore I command you, saying: You shall surely open your hand to your brother, to your poor, and to your needy, in your land.
If your brother, the Hebrew man, or the Hebrew woman, is sold to you, he shall serve you six years, and in the seventh year you shall send him free from you.
And when you send him free from you, you shall not send him away empty.
You shall surely furnish him from your flock, and from your threshing floor, and from your winepress; you shall give him from that with which Havayah your Elokim has blessed you.
And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Mitzrayim, and Havayah your Elokim redeemed you; therefore I command you this thing today.
And it shall be, if he says to you: I will not go out from you, because he loves you and your household, for it is good for him with you.
And you shall take the awl, and put it through his ear and into the door, and he shall be your servant forever; and also to your maidservant you shall do so.
It shall not be hard in your eyes when you send him free from you, for he served you six years, double the hire of a hired man, and Havayah your Elokim will bless you in all that you do.

You shall sanctify to Havayah your Elokim every firstborn male that is born of your cattle and of your flocks; you shall not work with the firstborn of your ox, and you shall not shear the firstborn of your flock.
Before Havayah your Elokim you shall eat it year by year, in the place that Havayah will choose, you and your household.
And if there is a blemish in it, lameness or blindness, any evil blemish, you shall not sacrifice it to Havayah your Elokim.
Within your gates you shall eat it, the impure and the pure alike, as the gazelle and as the deer.
Only its blood you shall not eat; upon the ground you shall pour it like water.
Keep the month of Aviv, and make a Pesach to Havayah your Elokim, for in the month of Aviv Havayah your Elokim brought you out of Mitzrayim by night.
And you shall slaughter a Pesach to Havayah your Elokim, flock and herd.

You shall not eat leavened bread with it; seven days you shall eat matzah with it, bread of affliction, for in haste you came out of the land of Mitzrayim, so that you will remember the day of your coming out of the land of Mitzrayim all the days of your life.
And no leaven shall be seen with you in all your borders seven days, and the flesh that you slaughter in the evening, on the first day, shall not remain overnight until morning.
You may not slaughter the Pesach within any of your gates that Havayah your Elokim is giving you.

But at the place that Havayah your Elokim will choose to rest His name, there you shall slaughter the Pesach in the evening, at the setting of the sun, the appointed time of your coming out of Mitzrayim.
And you shall cook and eat in the place that Havayah your Elokim will choose, and you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents.
Six days you shall eat matzah, and on the seventh day there shall be a solemn assembly to Havayah your Elokim; you shall do no work.
Seven weeks you shall count for yourself; from the beginning of the sickle in the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.
And you shall make the Festival of Weeks to Havayah your Elokim, with the freewill offering of your hand, which you shall give, as Havayah your Elokim blesses you.

And you shall rejoice before Havayah your Elokim, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your slave, and your maidservant, and the Levi who is within your gates, and the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow, who are in your midst, in the place that Havayah your Elokim will choose to rest His name there.
And you shall remember that you were a slave in Mitzrayim, and you shall keep and do these statutes.
You shall make the Festival of Sukkos seven days, when you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.

And you shall rejoice in your festival, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your slave, and your maidservant, and the Levi, and the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow, who are within your gates.

Seven days you shall celebrate to Havayah your Elokim, in the place that Havayah will choose, for Havayah your Elokim will bless you in all your crops, and in all the work of your hands, and you shall be wholly joyful.

Three times in the year all your males shall appear before Havayah your Elokim, in the place that He will choose, on the Festival of Matzos, and on the Festival of Weeks, and on the Festival of Sukkos, and they shall not appear before Havayah empty-handed.
Each man according to the gift of his hand, according to the blessing of Havayah your Elokim that He gave you.
You shall appoint judges and officers for yourself in all your gates that Havayah your Elokim is giving you, for your tribes, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
You shall not bend judgment; you shall not show favor, and you shall not take a bribe, for the bribe blinds the eyes of the wise, and twists the words of the righteous.
Justice, justice you shall pursue, so that you may live and possess the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you.
You shall not plant for yourself a sacred tree, any tree, beside the altar of Havayah your Elokim that you shall make for yourself.
And you shall not set up for yourself a standing stone, which Havayah your Elokim hates.
You shall not sacrifice to Havayah your Elokim an ox or a lamb, in which there is a blemish, any evil thing, for it is an abomination to Havayah your Elokim.
If there is found in your midst, within one of your gates that Havayah your Elokim is giving you, a man or a woman, who does evil in the eyes of Havayah your Elokim, to transgress His covenant.
And he goes and serves other gods, and bows to them, and to the sun, or to the moon, or to any of the host of the heavens, which I did not command.
And it is told to you, and you hear, and you inquire diligently, and behold, it is true, the matter is certain, this abomination was done in Yisroel.
And you shall bring out that man or that woman who did this evil thing to your gates, and stone them with stones, and they shall die.
The one to die shall be put to death by the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses; he shall not be put to death by the mouth of one witness.
The hand of the witnesses shall be upon him first, to put him to death, and the hand of all the people afterward, and you shall remove the evil from your midst.

If a matter is too hard for you in judgment, between blood and blood, between case and case, and between mark and mark, matters of dispute within your gates, you shall rise and go up to the place that Havayah your Elokim will choose.
And you shall come to the priests, the Leviim, and to the judge who shall be in those days, and you shall inquire, and they shall tell you the word of judgment.
And you shall do according to the word that they tell you, from that place that Havayah will choose, and you shall take care to do according to all that they instruct you.

According to the Torah that they instruct you, and according to the judgment that they say to you, you shall do; you shall not turn aside from the word that they tell you, to the right or to the left.
And the man who acts willfully, to not listen to the priest who stands to serve Havayah your Elokim there, or to the judge, that man shall die, and you shall remove the evil from Yisroel.
And all the people shall hear, and fear, and shall not act willfully anymore.
When you come to the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you, and possess it, and dwell in it, and you say: I will set a king over me, like all the nations that are around me.
You shall surely set a king over you, whom Havayah your Elokim will choose; from among your brothers you shall set a king over you; you may not set over you a foreign man, who is not your brother.
Only he shall not multiply horses for himself, and he shall not bring the people back to Mitzrayim, to multiply horses, for Havayah said to you: You shall not return on this way again.
And he shall not multiply wives for himself, and his heart shall not turn astray; and silver and gold he shall not multiply greatly for himself.
And it shall be, when he sits upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write for himself a copy of this Torah in a scroll, from before the priests, the Leviim.
And it shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear Havayah his Elokim, to keep all the words of this Torah and these statutes, to do them.

So that his heart is not lifted above his brothers, and so that he does not turn aside from the commandment, to the right or to the left, so that he may prolong his days over his kingdom, he and his sons, in the midst of Yisroel.
There shall not be for the priests, the Leviim, all the tribe of Levi, a portion and an inheritance with Yisroel; they shall eat the fire offerings of Havayah and His inheritance.
And he shall not have an inheritance among his brothers; Havayah is his inheritance, as He spoke to him.
And this shall be the due of the priests from the people, from those who slaughter a slaughtering, whether ox or lamb, and he shall give to the priest the foreleg, and the jaw, and the stomach.
You shall give him the first of your grain, and your wine, and your oil, and the first of the shearing of your flock.
For Havayah your Elokim has chosen him from all your tribes, to stand to serve in the name of Havayah, he and his sons, all the days.
And if a Levi comes from one of your gates, from all Yisroel, where he sojourns, and comes with all the desire of his soul to the place that Havayah will choose.
And he shall serve in the name of Havayah his Elokim, as all his brothers the Leviim, who stand there before Havayah.
Portion by portion they shall eat, besides that which was sold by the fathers.
When you come to the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you, you shall not learn to do according to the abominations of those nations.
There shall not be found among you one who passes his son or his daughter through fire, a sorcerer, or a soothsayer, or a diviner, or a warlock.
Or an enchanter, or a medium, or an oracle, or a necromancer.
For anyone who does these is an abomination to Havayah, and because of these abominations Havayah your Elokim drives them out from before you.
You shall be wholehearted with Havayah your Elokim.
For these nations that you are dispossessing listen to soothsayers and to sorcerers, but you — not so has Havayah your Elokim given to you.
Havayah your Elokim will raise up for you a prophet from your midst, from your brothers, like me; him you shall heed.

According to all that you asked of Havayah your Elokim at Chorev, on the day of the assembly, saying: I shall not continue to hear the voice of Havayah my Elokim, and I shall not see this great fire again, so that I do not die.
And Havayah said to me: They have done well in what they spoke.
I will raise up a prophet for them from among their brothers, like you, and I will put My words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him.
And it shall be, the man who does not listen to My words that he speaks in My name, I will require it of him.
But the prophet who acts willfully to speak a word in My name that I did not command him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.
And if you say in your heart: How shall we know the word that Havayah did not speak?

That which the prophet speaks in the name of Havayah, and the thing is not, and it does not come, that is the word that Havayah did not speak; with willfulness the prophet spoke it; you shall not fear him.
When Havayah your Elokim cuts off the nations that Havayah your Elokim is giving you their land, and you dispossess them, and dwell in their cities and in their houses.
You shall set apart three cities for yourself, in the midst of your land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you to possess.
You shall prepare the road for yourself, and divide into three parts the border of your land that Havayah your Elokim will give you as an inheritance, and it shall be for every killer to flee there.
And this is the matter of the killer who shall flee there and live: who strikes his neighbor without knowledge, and he did not hate him from yesterday or the day before.

And who comes with his neighbor into the forest to cut wood, and his hand swings with the axe to cut the tree, and the iron slips from the wood, and finds his neighbor, and he dies, he shall flee to one of these cities and live.

Lest the avenger of blood pursue the killer, when his heart is hot, and overtake him, because the way is long, and strike him mortally, and he has no sentence of death, for he did not hate him from yesterday or the day before.
Therefore I command you, saying: You shall set apart three cities for yourself.
And if Havayah your Elokim enlarges your border, as He swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land that He spoke to give to your fathers.

If you keep all this commandment to do it, that I command you today, to love Havayah your Elokim, and to walk in His ways all the days, then you shall add for yourself three more cities, besides these three.
And innocent blood shall not be shed in the midst of your land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you as an inheritance, and blood shall not be upon you.
And if there is a man who hates his neighbor, and lies in wait for him, and rises against him, and strikes him mortally, and he dies, and he flees to one of these cities.
And the elders of his city shall send and take him from there, and give him into the hand of the avenger of blood, and he shall die.
Your eye shall not pity him, and you shall remove the innocent blood from Yisroel, and it shall be good for you.
You shall not move the boundary of your neighbor, which the first ones marked, in your inheritance that you shall inherit, in the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you to possess.
One witness shall not rise against a man for any iniquity or for any sin, in any sin that he sins; a matter shall be established by the mouth of two witnesses, or by the mouth of three witnesses.
If a corrupt witness rises against a man, to testify against him a falsehood.
And the two men who have the dispute shall stand before Havayah, before the priests and the judges who shall be in those days.
And the judges shall search diligently, and behold, a false witness is the witness; he testified falsehood against his brother.
And you shall do to him as he schemed to do to his brother, and you shall remove the evil from your midst.
And those who remain shall hear, and fear, and shall not do again like this evil thing in your midst.
And your eye shall not pity; life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

When you go out to war against your enemies, and you see horses and chariots, a more numerous people than you, you shall not fear them, for Havayah your Elokim is with you, who brought you up from the land of Mitzrayim.
And it shall be, when you draw near to the war, the priest shall approach and speak to the people.
And he shall say to them: Hear, Yisroel, you are drawing near today to war against your enemies; let your heart not be faint, do not fear, and do not panic, and do not be broken before them.
For Havayah your Elokim goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.

And the officers shall speak to the people, saying: Who is the man who built a new house, and did not dedicate it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the war, and another man dedicate it.
And who is the man who planted a vineyard, and did not enjoy it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the war, and another man enjoy it.
And who is the man who betrothed a woman, and did not take her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the war, and another man take her.

And the officers shall speak further to the people, and say: Who is the man who is fearful and fainthearted? Let him go and return to his house, and let him not melt the heart of his brothers, as his heart.
And it shall be, when the officers finish speaking to the people, they shall appoint commanders of the armies at the head of the people.
When you draw near to a city to fight against it, you shall call out to it for peace.
And it shall be, if it answers you peace, and opens to you, then all the people found in it shall be for tribute to you, and they shall serve you.
And if it does not make peace with you, and makes war with you, you shall besiege it.
