And Havayah your Elokim will give it into your hand, and you shall strike all its males by the sword.

You shall take as plunder for yourself only the women, and the little children, and the cattle, and all that is in the city, all its spoil, and you shall eat the spoil of your enemies that Havayah your Elokim has given you.
So you shall do to all the cities that are very far from you, that are not of the cities of these nations.
But of the cities of these peoples that Havayah your Elokim is giving you as an inheritance, you shall not keep alive any soul.
But you shall utterly destroy them, the Chiti, and the Emori, the Kena'ani, and the Perizi, the Chivi, and the Yevusi, as Havayah your Elokim commanded you.
So that they do not teach you to do according to all their abominations that they did for their gods, and you sin against Havayah your Elokim.
When you besiege a city many days, to fight against it, to take it, you shall not destroy its trees, to raise an axe against them, for from them you eat, and you shall not cut them down.
Only a tree that you know is not a food tree, you may destroy it and cut it down, and build a siege against the city that makes war with you, until it falls.
If a slain man is found in the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you to possess, fallen in the field, and it is not known who struck him.
And your elders and your judges shall go out, and measure to the cities that are around the slain man.
And it shall be, the city that is nearest to the slain man, the elders of that city shall take a heifer, with which no work has been done, which has not pulled in a yoke.
And the elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to a rugged ravine, which is not worked and not sown, and break the neck of the heifer there in the ravine.
And the priests, the sons of Levi, shall approach, for Havayah your Elokim chose them to serve Him, and to bless in the name of Havayah, and every dispute and every affliction shall be by their word.
And all the elders of that city, who are nearest to the slain man, shall wash their hands over the heifer that was beheaded in the ravine.
And they shall answer and say: Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see.
Atone for Your people Yisroel, whom You redeemed, Havayah, and do not place innocent blood in the midst of Your people Yisroel, and the blood shall be atoned for them.
And you shall remove the innocent blood from your midst, when you do the right in the eyes of Havayah.
When you go out to war against your enemies, and Havayah your Elokim gives them into your hand, and you take captives from them.
And you see among the captives a beautiful woman, and you desire her, and take her for yourself as a wife.
And you shall bring her into your house, and she shall shave her head, and do her nails.

And she shall take off the garment of her captivity from her, and dwell in your house, and mourn her father and her mother a full month, and afterward you may come to her, and be her husband, and she shall be your wife.
And it shall be, if you do not desire her, you shall send her away on her own, and you shall not sell her for silver; you shall not enslave her, because you afflicted her.
If a man has two wives, one beloved and one hated, and they bear him sons, the beloved and the hated, and the firstborn son is the hated one's.
It shall be, on the day he bequeaths to his sons what he has, he may not make the son of the beloved the firstborn, over the son of the hated, who is the firstborn.
But the firstborn, the son of the hated, he shall acknowledge, to give him a double portion of all that is found with him, for he is the first of his strength; his is the right of the firstborn.
If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son, who does not listen to the voice of his father, and the voice of his mother, and they chastise him, and he does not listen to them.
And his father and his mother shall take hold of him, and bring him out to the elders of his city, and to the gate of his place.
And they shall say to the elders of his city: This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he does not listen to our voice; he is a glutton and a drunkard.
And all the men of his city shall stone him with stones, and he shall die, and you shall remove the evil from your midst, and all Yisroel shall hear and fear.
And if a man has a sin, a judgment of death, and he is put to death, and you hang him on a tree.

His body shall not remain overnight on the tree, but you shall surely bury him on that day, for the hanged one is a curse of Elokim, and you shall not defile your land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you as an inheritance.
You shall not see your brother's ox or his sheep straying, and ignore them; you shall surely return them to your brother.
And if your brother is not near to you, and you do not know him, you shall bring it into your house, and it shall be with you until your brother seeks it, and you shall return it to him.
And so you shall do with his donkey, and so you shall do with his garment, and so you shall do with every lost thing of your brother, that is lost from him and you find; you shall not ignore it.
You shall not see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen on the road, and ignore them; you shall surely raise it with him.
A man's garment shall not be upon a woman, and a man shall not wear a woman's garment, for anyone who does these is an abomination to Havayah your Elokim.
If a bird's nest chances before you on the way, on any tree or on the ground, young or eggs, and the mother is sitting upon the young or upon the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the young.
You shall surely send away the mother, and you may take the young for yourself, so that it will be good for you, and you will prolong your days.
When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, and you shall not place blood upon your house, if one falls from it.
You shall not sow your vineyard with mixed kinds, lest the growth be forbidden, the seed that you sow and the yield of the vineyard.
You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together.
You shall not wear shaatnez, wool and linen together.
You shall make twisted threads for yourself, on the four corners of your garment, with which you cover yourself.
If a man takes a wife, and comes to her, and hates her.
And he puts against her a false charge, and spreads an evil name about her, and says: I took this woman, and I came to her, and I did not find virginity in her.
And the father of the young woman and her mother shall take and bring out the signs of the virginity of the young woman, to the elders of the city, to the gate.
And the father of the young woman shall say to the elders: I gave my daughter to this man for a wife, and he hates her.

And behold, he put a false charge, saying: I did not find in your daughter virginity; and these are the signs of virginity of my daughter. And they shall spread the garment before the elders of the city.
And the elders of that city shall take the man, and chastise him.

And they shall fine him one hundred shekels of silver, and give it to the father of the young woman, because he spread an evil name about a virgin of Yisroel; and she shall be his wife; he may not send her away all his days.
And if this matter was true, virginity was not found for the young woman.

And they shall bring the young woman out to the door of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones, and she shall die, for she did a disgraceful thing in Yisroel, to play the harlot in her father's house, and you shall remove the evil from your midst.
If a man is found lying with a woman married to a husband, both of them shall die, the man who lay with the woman, and the woman, and you shall remove the evil from Yisroel.
If there is a young virgin betrothed to a man, and a man finds her in the city, and lies with her.

And you shall bring them both out to the gate of that city, and stone them with stones, and they shall die, the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he afflicted the wife of his neighbor, and you shall remove the evil from your midst.
And if the man finds the betrothed young woman in the field, and the man seizes her and lies with her, the man who lay with her shall die alone.
And to the young woman you shall do nothing; the young woman has no sin of death, for as a man rises against his neighbor and murders him, so is this matter.
For he found her in the field; the betrothed young woman cried out, and there was no savior for her.
If a man finds a young virgin who is not betrothed, and seizes her and lies with her, and they are found.
And the man who lay with her shall give to the father of the young woman fifty shekels of silver, and she shall be his wife, because he afflicted her; he may not send her away all his days.
A man shall not take his father's wife, and he shall not uncover the edge of his father's garment.
One with crushed testicles, and one with a severed member, shall not enter the assembly of Havayah.
A mamzer shall not enter the assembly of Havayah; even his tenth generation shall not enter the assembly of Havayah.
An Ammoni and a Moavi shall not enter the assembly of Havayah; even their tenth generation shall not enter the assembly of Havayah, forever.
Because they did not meet you with bread and with water on the way, in your coming out of Mitzrayim, and because he hired against you Bilam son of Beor, from Petor, Aram Naharayim, to curse you.
And Havayah your Elokim did not want to listen to Bilam, and Havayah your Elokim turned the curse into a blessing for you, because Havayah your Elokim loves you.
You shall not seek their peace and their welfare, all your days, forever.
You shall not despise an Edomi, for he is your brother; you shall not despise a Mitzri, for you were a stranger in his land.
Children that are born to them, in the third generation, shall enter the assembly of Havayah.
When you go out in a camp against your enemies, you shall guard yourself from every evil thing.
If there is among you a man who is not pure, from a nocturnal occurrence, he shall go out of the camp; he shall not come into the midst of the camp.
And it shall be, toward evening he shall bathe in water, and when the sun sets, he shall come into the camp.
And a place shall be for you outside the camp, and you shall go out there.
And a spade shall be for you with your weapons, and it shall be, when you sit outside, you shall dig with it, and return and cover your excrement.

For Havayah your Elokim walks in the midst of your camp, to save you, and to give your enemies before you, and your camp shall be holy, so that He does not see a shameful thing among you, and turn away from you.
You shall not hand over a slave to his master, who flees to you from his master.
With you he shall dwell, in your midst, in the place that he chooses, within one of your gates, where it is good for him; you shall not oppress him.
There shall not be a prostitute from the daughters of Yisroel, and there shall not be a male prostitute from the sons of Yisroel.
You shall not bring the fee of a harlot, or the price of a dog, to the House of Havayah your Elokim, for any vow, for both of them are an abomination to Havayah your Elokim.
You shall not lend with interest to your brother, interest of silver, interest of food, interest of anything that is lent with interest.

To the foreigner you may lend with interest, and to your brother you shall not lend with interest, so that Havayah your Elokim will bless you in all the sending forth of your hand, in the land that you are coming there to possess.
When you vow a vow to Havayah your Elokim, you shall not delay to pay it, for Havayah your Elokim will surely require it of you, and it will be a sin in you.
If you refrain from vowing, there shall be no sin in you.
What comes out of your lips you shall keep and do, as you vowed a freewill offering to Havayah your Elokim, that you spoke with your mouth.
When you come into your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat grapes as your soul desires, to your fill, but you shall not put any into your vessel.
When you come into your neighbor's standing grain, you may pick ears with your hand, but you shall not swing a sickle over your neighbor's standing grain.

When a man takes a wife, and marries her, and it is that she does not find favor in his eyes, because he found in her an unseemly matter, and he writes her a bill of divorce, and gives it in her hand, and sends her from his house.
And she goes out of his house, and goes, and becomes another man's wife.
And the second man hates her, and writes her a bill of divorce, and gives it in her hand, and sends her from his house, or if the second man dies, who took her for himself as a wife.

Her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after she has been defiled, for it is an abomination before Havayah, and you shall not bring sin upon the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you as an inheritance.
When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out to war, and he shall not be charged with any matter; he shall be free for his house one year, and shall make his wife, whom he took, rejoice.
One shall not take as pledge a millstone and an upper millstone, for he takes a life as pledge.
If a man is found kidnapping a soul from his brothers, from the children of Yisroel, and enslaves him and sells him, that thief shall die, and you shall remove the evil from your midst.
Take care with the mark of tzaraas, to observe greatly, and to do according to all that the priests, the Leviim, instruct you; as I commanded them, you shall take care to do.
Remember what Havayah your Elokim did to Miriam, on the way, in your coming out of Mitzrayim.
When you lend your neighbor a loan of anything, you shall not go into his house to take his pledge.
You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you lend shall bring the pledge out to you outside.
And if he is a poor man, you shall not sleep with his pledge.
You shall surely return the pledge to him at the setting of the sun, and he shall sleep in his garment, and bless you, and it shall be righteousness for you before Havayah your Elokim.
You shall not oppress a poor and needy hired laborer, from your brothers, or from your stranger who is in your land within your gates.
On his day you shall give his wage, and the sun shall not set upon it, for he is poor, and he sets his soul upon it, lest he cry against you to Havayah, and it be a sin in you.
Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, and sons shall not be put to death for fathers; each man for his own sin shall be put to death.
You shall not bend the judgment of a stranger or an orphan, and you shall not take a widow's garment as a pledge.
And you shall remember that you were a slave in Mitzrayim, and Havayah your Elokim redeemed you from there; therefore I command you to do this thing.

When you reap your harvest in your field, and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not return to take it; it shall be for the stranger, for the orphan, and for the widow, so that Havayah your Elokim will bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the branches after you; it shall be for the stranger, for the orphan, and for the widow.
When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not glean after you; it shall be for the stranger, for the orphan, and for the widow.
And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Mitzrayim; therefore I command you to do this thing.
When there is a dispute between men, and they approach judgment, and they judge them, and declare the righteous righteous, and declare the wicked wicked.
And it shall be, if the wicked man is worthy of being beaten, the judge shall have him lie down, and flog him before him, by number, according to his wickedness.
He shall flog him forty lashes; he shall not add, lest he add to flog him beyond these a great blow, and your brother be degraded before your eyes.
You shall not muzzle an ox in its threshing.

If brothers dwell together, and one of them dies, and he has no son, the wife of the dead shall not be outside, to a strange man; her husband's brother shall come to her, and take her for himself as a wife, and perform levirate marriage with her.
And it shall be, the firstborn that she bears shall stand in the name of his brother who died, and his name shall not be wiped out from Yisroel.

And if the man does not wish to take his brother's widow, his brother's widow shall go up to the gate, to the elders, and say: My husband's brother refuses to raise up a name for his brother in Yisroel; he will not perform levirate marriage with me.
And the elders of his city shall call him, and speak to him, and he shall stand and say: I do not wish to take her.

And his brother's widow shall approach him before the eyes of the elders, and remove his shoe from his foot, and spit before him, and answer and say: So shall be done to the man who will not build the house of his brother.
And his name shall be called in Yisroel: The house of him whose shoe was removed.

If men fight together, a man and his brother, and the wife of one approaches to save her husband from the hand of the one who strikes him, and she stretches out her hand, and seizes his private parts.
And you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not pity her.
You shall not have in your pouch a weight and a weight, a large and a small.
You shall not have in your house a measure and a measure, a large and a small.
You shall have a whole and just weight; you shall have a whole and just measure, so that your days may be long upon the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you.
For anyone who does these, anyone who does injustice, is an abomination to Havayah your Elokim.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the way, in your coming out of Mitzrayim.
How he met you on the way, and struck from behind you all the stragglers behind you, when you were faint and weary, and he did not fear Elokim.

And it shall be, when Havayah your Elokim gives you rest from all your enemies around you, in the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you as an inheritance to possess, you shall wipe out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens; you shall not forget.
And it shall be, when you come to the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you as an inheritance, and you possess it, and dwell in it.

And you shall take from the first of all the fruit of the ground, that you bring from your land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you, and place it in a basket, and go to the place that Havayah your Elokim will choose to rest His name there.
And you shall come to the priest who shall be in those days, and say to him: I declare today to Havayah your Elokim that I have come to the land that Havayah swore to our fathers to give to us.
And the priest shall take the basket from your hand, and set it down before the altar of Havayah your Elokim.

And you shall answer and say before Havayah your Elokim: My father was a wandering Arami, and he went down to Mitzrayim, and sojourned there with few people, and became there a great, mighty, and numerous nation.
And the Mitzrim treated us ill, and afflicted us, and laid hard labor upon us.
And we cried out to Havayah, Elokim of our fathers, and Havayah heard our voice, and saw our affliction, and our toil, and our oppression.
And Havayah brought us out of Mitzrayim with a mighty hand, and with an outstretched arm, and with great terror, and with signs, and with wonders.
And He brought us to this place, and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now, behold, I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground that You gave me, Havayah. And you shall set it down before Havayah your Elokim, and bow down before Havayah your Elokim.
And you shall rejoice in all the good that Havayah your Elokim has given you and your household, you, and the Levi, and the stranger who is in your midst.

When you finish tithing all the tithes of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, and you have given it to the Levi, to the stranger, to the orphan, and to the widow, and they ate within your gates, and were satisfied.

And you shall say before Havayah your Elokim: I have removed the holy things from my house, and I have given them to the Levi, and to the stranger, to the orphan, and to the widow, according to all Your commandment that You commanded me; I did not transgress Your commandments, and I did not forget.

I did not eat of it in my mourning, and I did not remove of it while impure, and I did not give of it for the dead; I listened to the voice of Havayah my Elokim; I did according to all that You commanded me.
Look down from Your holy dwelling, from the heavens, and bless Your people Yisroel, and the land that You gave us, as You swore to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.
This day Havayah your Elokim commands you to do these statutes and these ordinances, and you shall keep and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
You have declared Havayah today to be your Elokim, and to walk in His ways, and to keep His statutes, and His commandments, and His ordinances, and to listen to His voice.
And Havayah has declared you today to be His treasured people, as He spoke to you, and to keep all His commandments.
And to set you highest above all the nations that He made, for praise, and for renown, and for splendor, and for you to be a holy people to Havayah your Elokim, as He spoke.
And Moshe and the elders of Yisroel commanded the people, saying: Keep all the commandment that I command you today.
And it shall be, on the day you cross the Yarden to the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you, you shall set up for yourself great stones, and plaster them with lime.

And you shall write upon them all the words of this Torah, in your crossing over, so that you come to the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as Havayah, Elokim of your fathers, spoke to you.
And it shall be, when you cross the Yarden, you shall set up these stones that I command you today, on Mount Eival, and you shall plaster them with lime.
And you shall build there an altar to Havayah your Elokim, an altar of stones; you shall not lift iron upon them.
You shall build the altar of Havayah your Elokim of whole stones, and you shall offer upon it burnt offerings to Havayah your Elokim.
And you shall slaughter peace offerings, and eat there, and rejoice before Havayah your Elokim.
And you shall write upon the stones all the words of this Torah, very clearly.
And Moshe and the priests, the Leviim, spoke to all Yisroel, saying: Be silent and listen, Yisroel; this day you have become a people to Havayah your Elokim.
And you shall listen to the voice of Havayah your Elokim, and do His commandments and His statutes that I command you today.
And Moshe commanded the people on that day, saying.
These shall stand to bless the people upon Mount Gerizim, in your crossing the Yarden: Shimon, and Levi, and Yehudah, and Yissachar, and Yosef, and Binyamin.
And these shall stand for the curse upon Mount Eival: Reuven, Gad, and Asher, and Zevulun, Dan, and Naftali.
And the Leviim shall answer and say to every man of Yisroel, with a loud voice.
Cursed is the man who makes a carved image or a cast figure, an abomination to Havayah, the work of the hands of a craftsman, and sets it in secret. And all the people shall answer and say: Amen.
Cursed is one who dishonors his father or his mother. And all the people shall say: Amen.
Cursed is one who moves the boundary of his neighbor. And all the people shall say: Amen.
Cursed is one who leads the blind astray on the way. And all the people shall say: Amen.
Cursed is one who bends the judgment of the stranger, the orphan, and the widow. And all the people shall say: Amen.
Cursed is one who lies with his father's wife, for he uncovered the edge of his father's garment. And all the people shall say: Amen.
Cursed is one who lies with any beast. And all the people shall say: Amen.
Cursed is one who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. And all the people shall say: Amen.
Cursed is one who lies with his mother-in-law. And all the people shall say: Amen.
Cursed is one who strikes his neighbor in secret. And all the people shall say: Amen.
Cursed is one who takes a bribe to strike a soul, innocent blood. And all the people shall say: Amen.
Cursed is one who does not uphold the words of this Torah, to do them. And all the people shall say: Amen.

And it shall be, if you listen to the voice of Havayah your Elokim, to take care to do all His commandments that I command you today, Havayah your Elokim will set you highest above all the nations of the earth.
And all these blessings will come upon you, and overtake you, if you listen to the voice of Havayah your Elokim.
Blessed are you in the city, and blessed are you in the field.
Blessed is the fruit of your womb, and the fruit of your land, and the fruit of your animals, the calving of your cattle, and the lambing of your flock.
Blessed is your basket, and your kneading bowl.
Blessed are you in your coming in, and blessed are you in your going out.
Havayah will make your enemies who rise against you fall defeated before you; by one road they will come out toward you, and by seven roads they will flee before you.
Havayah will command the blessing upon you in your storehouses, and in all the sending forth of your hand, and He will bless you in the land that Havayah your Elokim is giving you.
Havayah will establish you as a holy people to Him, as He swore to you, if you keep the commandments of Havayah your Elokim, and walk in His ways.
And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of Havayah is called upon you, and they shall fear you.
And Havayah will give you abundance for good, in the fruit of your womb, and in the fruit of your animals, and in the fruit of your land, upon the land that Havayah swore to your fathers to give you.

Havayah will open for you His good storehouse, the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its season, and to bless all the work of your hand, and you shall lend to many nations, and you shall not borrow.

And Havayah will make you the head, and not the tail, and you shall be only above, and you shall not be below, if you listen to the commandments of Havayah your Elokim that I command you today, to keep and to do them.
And you shall not turn aside from all the words that I command you today, to the right or to the left, to go after other gods, to serve them.

And it shall be, if you do not listen to the voice of Havayah your Elokim, to take care to do all His commandments and His statutes that I command you today, all these curses will come upon you, and overtake you.
Cursed are you in the city, and cursed are you in the field.
Cursed is your basket, and your kneading bowl.
Cursed is the fruit of your womb, and the fruit of your land, the calving of your cattle, and the lambing of your flock.
Cursed are you in your coming in, and cursed are you in your going out.

Havayah will send among you the curse, the confusion, and the rebuke, in all the sending forth of your hand that you do, until you are destroyed, and until you perish quickly, because of the evil of your deeds, that you forsook Me.
Havayah will make the pestilence cling to you, until He consumes you from the land that you are coming there to possess.

Havayah will strike you with wasting disease, and with fever, and with inflammation, and with burning heat, and with the sword, and with blight, and with mildew, and they shall pursue you until you perish.
And your heavens that are over your head shall be bronze, and the earth that is under you shall be iron.
Havayah will make the rain of your land dust and dirt; from the heavens it shall come down upon you, until you are destroyed.

Havayah will make you fall defeated before your enemies; by one road you shall go out toward him, and by seven roads you shall flee before him, and you shall be a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
And your corpse shall be food for every bird of the heavens, and for the animals of the earth, and there shall be none to frighten them.
Havayah will strike you with the boils of Mitzrayim, and with hemorrhoids, and with scabs, and with itching, from which you cannot be healed.
Havayah will strike you with madness, and with blindness, and with bewilderment of heart.
And you shall grope at noon, as the blind gropes in the darkness, and you shall not prosper in your ways, and you shall be only oppressed and robbed all the days, and there shall be no savior.
You shall betroth a woman, and another man shall lie with her; you shall build a house, and you shall not dwell in it; you shall plant a vineyard, and you shall not enjoy it.

Your ox is slaughtered before your eyes, and you shall not eat of it; your donkey is taken from before you, and shall not return to you; your flock is given to your enemies, and there is no savior for you.
Your sons and your daughters are given to another people, and your eyes see and long for them all the day, and there is no power in your hand.
A nation that you did not know shall eat the fruit of your land and all your labor, and you shall be only oppressed and crushed all the days.
And you shall be mad from the sight of your eyes that you shall see.
Havayah will strike you with a grievous boil on the knees and on the legs, from which you cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.
Havayah will bring you, and your king whom you set over you, to a nation that you did not know, you and your fathers, and you shall serve there other gods, wood and stone.
And you shall become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all the peoples where Havayah shall lead you.
You shall carry much seed out to the field, and gather little, for the locust shall consume it.
You shall plant and tend vineyards, and you shall not drink wine, and you shall not gather, for the worm shall eat it.
You shall have olive trees within all your borders, and you shall not anoint yourself with oil, for your olives shall drop off.
You shall beget sons and daughters, and they shall not be for you, for they shall go into captivity.
The locust shall consume all your trees and the fruit of your land.
The stranger who is in your midst shall rise above you, higher and higher, and you shall go down, lower and lower.
He shall lend to you, and you shall not lend to him; he shall be the head, and you shall be the tail.

And all these curses shall come upon you, and pursue you, and overtake you, until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of Havayah your Elokim, to keep His commandments and His statutes that He commanded you.
And they shall be upon you for a sign and for a wonder, and upon your seed forever.
Because you did not serve Havayah your Elokim with joy and with gladness of heart, from abundance of everything.

And you shall serve your enemies, whom Havayah shall send against you, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in lack of everything, and he shall put a yoke of iron upon your neck, until he destroys you.
Havayah will bring a nation against you from afar, from the end of the earth, as the eagle swoops, a nation whose tongue you shall not understand.
A brazen nation, which shall not show favor to the old, and shall not have mercy on the young.

And it shall eat the fruit of your animals and the fruit of your land, until you are destroyed, which shall not leave you grain, wine, or oil, calving of your cattle, or lambing of your flock, until it destroys you.

And it shall besiege you at all your gates, until your high and fortified walls come down, in which you trusted, in all your land, and it shall besiege you at all your gates, in all your land that Havayah your Elokim has given you.
And you shall eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and your daughters, that Havayah your Elokim gave you, in the siege and in the distress that your enemy shall distress you.
The man among you who is tender and very delicate, his eye shall be evil toward his brother, and toward the wife of his bosom, and toward the remnant of his children that he has left.
From giving to one of them of the flesh of his children that he eats, because nothing is left to him, in the siege and in the distress that your enemy shall distress you in all your gates.

The tender and delicate woman among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot upon the ground, for delicateness and for tenderness, her eye shall be evil toward the husband of her bosom, and toward her son, and toward her daughter.

And toward her afterbirth that comes out from between her feet, and toward her children that she bears, for she shall eat them in lack of everything, in secret, in the siege and in the distress that your enemy shall distress you in your gates.
If you do not take care to do all the words of this Torah, that are written in this book, to fear this honored and awesome name, Havayah your Elokim.
Then Havayah will make your blows extraordinary, and the blows of your seed, great and lasting blows, and grievous and lasting sicknesses.
And He will bring back upon you all the diseases of Mitzrayim, of which you were afraid, and they shall cling to you.
Havayah will also bring upon you every sickness and every blow that is not written in the book of this Torah, until you are destroyed.
And you shall be left few in number, instead of your being as the stars of the heavens for multitude, because you did not listen to the voice of Havayah your Elokim.

And it shall be, as Havayah rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you, so Havayah will rejoice over you to destroy you, and to wipe you out, and you shall be torn away from the land that you are coming there to possess.

And Havayah will scatter you among all the peoples, from the end of the earth to the end of the earth, and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone, that you did not know, you and your fathers.

And among those nations you shall find no rest, and there shall be no resting place for the sole of your foot, and Havayah will give you there a trembling heart, and failing eyes, and a languishing soul.
And your life shall hang in doubt before you, and you shall fear night and day, and you shall have no assurance of your life.

In the morning you shall say: Would that it were evening, and in the evening you shall say: Would that it were morning, from the fear of your heart that you shall fear, and from the sight of your eyes that you shall see.

And Havayah will bring you back to Mitzrayim in ships, by the way that I said to you: You shall not see it again, and there you shall offer yourselves for sale to your enemies, as slaves and as maidservants, and there shall be no buyer.
These are the words of the covenant that Havayah commanded Moshe to make with the children of Yisroel, in the land of Moav, besides the covenant that He made with them at Chorev.
And Moshe called all Yisroel, and said to them: You have seen all that Havayah did before your eyes in the land of Mitzrayim, to Paroh, and to all his servants, and to all his land.
The great trials that your eyes saw, the signs and those great wonders.
And Havayah has not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, until this day.
And I led you forty years in the wilderness; your garments did not wear out upon you, and your shoe did not wear out upon your foot.
You did not eat bread, and you did not drink wine and strong drink, so that you will know that I am Havayah your Elokim.
And you came to this place, and Sichon, king of Cheshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, came out toward us to war, and we smote them.
And we took their land, and gave it as an inheritance to the Reuvenites, and to the Gadites, and to half the tribe of Menasheh.
And you shall keep the words of this covenant, and do them, so that you will prosper in all that you do.
You are standing today, all of you, before Havayah your Elokim, your heads, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, every man of Yisroel.
Your little ones, your wives, and your stranger who is in the midst of your camp, from the hewer of your wood to the drawer of your water.
To enter into the covenant of Havayah your Elokim, and into His oath, that Havayah your Elokim is making with you today.
In order to establish you today as a people for Him, and He will be Elokim to you, as He spoke to you, and as He swore to your fathers, to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yackov.
And not with you alone do I make this covenant and this oath.
But with him who is here with us standing today before Havayah our Elokim, and with him who is not here with us today.
For you know how we dwelled in the land of Mitzrayim, and how we passed in the midst of the nations that you passed.
And you saw their abominations, and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, that are with them.

Lest there be among you a man, or a woman, or a family, or a tribe, whose heart turns today from Havayah our Elokim, to go to serve the gods of those nations, lest there be among you a root bearing gall and wormwood.
And it shall be, when he hears the words of this oath, he blesses himself in his heart, saying: Peace shall be mine, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart, to add the watered to the dry.

Havayah will not be willing to forgive him, for then the anger of Havayah and His jealousy shall smoke against that man, and all the curse that is written in this book shall rest upon him, and Havayah will wipe out his name from under the heavens.
And Havayah will set him apart for evil, from all the tribes of Yisroel, according to all the curses of the covenant that is written in this book of the Torah.

And the later generation, your children who rise after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land, shall say, when they see the afflictions of that land, and its sicknesses, with which Havayah has struck it.

Sulfur and salt, its whole land is burned; it shall not be sown, and it shall not sprout, and no grass shall grow in it, like the overturning of Sedom and Amorah, Admah and Tzevoyim, which Havayah overturned in His anger and in His fury.
And all the nations shall say: Why did Havayah do so to this land? What is this great burning anger?
And they shall say: Because they forsook the covenant of Havayah, Elokim of their fathers, which He made with them in His bringing them out of the land of Mitzrayim.
And they went and served other gods, and bowed to them, gods that they did not know, and He did not apportion to them.
And the anger of Havayah burned against that land, to bring upon it all the curse that is written in this book.
And Havayah uprooted them from upon their land, in anger, and in fury, and in great rage, and cast them to another land, as this day.
The hidden things belong to Havayah our Elokim, and the revealed things belong to us and to our children forever, to do all the words of this Torah.

And it shall be, when all these things come upon you, the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, you shall take it to heart, among all the nations where Havayah your Elokim has driven you.
And you shall return to Havayah your Elokim, and listen to His voice, according to all that I command you today, you and your children, with all your heart and with all your soul.
And Havayah your Elokim will bring back your captives, and have mercy on you, and return and gather you from all the peoples where Havayah your Elokim scattered you.
If your outcasts are at the ends of the heavens, from there Havayah your Elokim will gather you, and from there He will take you.
And Havayah your Elokim will bring you to the land that your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it, and He will do good to you, and multiply you more than your fathers.
And Havayah your Elokim will circumcise your heart, and the heart of your seed, to love Havayah your Elokim with all your heart and with all your soul, for the sake of your life.
And Havayah your Elokim will put all these curses upon your enemies, and upon those who hate you, who pursued you.
And you shall return, and listen to the voice of Havayah, and do all His commandments that I command you today.

And Havayah your Elokim will make you abound in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your womb, and in the fruit of your animals, and in the fruit of your land, for good, for Havayah will again rejoice over you for good, as He rejoiced over your fathers.

If you listen to the voice of Havayah your Elokim, to keep His commandments and His statutes, that are written in this book of the Torah, when you return to Havayah your Elokim with all your heart and with all your soul.
For this commandment that I command you today, it is not hidden from you, and it is not far off.
It is not in the heavens, that you should say: Who will go up for us to the heavens, and take it for us, and tell it to us, that we may do it?
And it is not beyond the sea, that you should say: Who will cross for us to the other side of the sea, and take it for us, and tell it to us, that we may do it?
For the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.
See, I have set before you today life and good, and death and evil.

That I command you today to love Havayah your Elokim, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments, and His statutes, and His ordinances, and you shall live and multiply, and Havayah your Elokim will bless you in the land that you are coming there to possess.
And if your heart turns away, and you do not listen, and you are drawn astray, and you bow to other gods, and serve them.
I tell you today that you shall surely perish; you shall not prolong your days upon the land that you are crossing the Yarden to come there to possess.
I call to witness against you today the heavens and the earth: I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse, and you shall choose life, so that you and your seed may live.

To love Havayah your Elokim, to listen to His voice, and to cleave to Him, for He is your life and the length of your days, to dwell upon the land that Havayah swore to your fathers, to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yackov, to give to them.
And Moshe went and spoke these words to all Yisroel.
And he said to them: I am one hundred and twenty years old today; I can no longer go out and come in, and Havayah said to me: You shall not cross this Yarden.
Havayah your Elokim, He is crossing before you; He will destroy these nations from before you, and you shall possess them; Yehoshua, he is crossing before you, as Havayah spoke.
And Havayah will do to them as He did to Sichon and to Og, kings of the Emorim, and to their land, whom He destroyed.
And Havayah will give them before you, and you shall do to them according to all the commandment that I commanded you.
Be strong and of good courage; do not fear, and do not be dismayed before them, for Havayah your Elokim, it is He who goes with you; He will not let go of you, and He will not forsake you.

And Moshe called Yehoshua, and said to him before the eyes of all Yisroel: Be strong and of good courage, for you shall come with this people to the land that Havayah swore to their fathers to give them, and you shall cause them to inherit it.
And Havayah, it is He who goes before you; He will be with you; He will not let go of you, and He will not forsake you; do not fear, and do not be dismayed.
And Moshe wrote this Torah, and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carry the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah, and to all the elders of Yisroel.
And Moshe commanded them, saying: At the end of seven years, in the appointed time of the year of release, on the Festival of Sukkos.
When all Yisroel comes to appear before Havayah your Elokim, in the place that He will choose, you shall read this Torah before all Yisroel, in their ears.

Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones, and your stranger who is within your gates, so that they hear, and so that they learn, and fear Havayah your Elokim, and take care to do all the words of this Torah.
And their children who do not know shall hear, and learn to fear Havayah your Elokim, all the days that you live upon the land that you are crossing the Yarden there to possess.

And Havayah said to Moshe: Behold, your days are drawing near to die; call Yehoshua, and stand in the Tent of Meeting, and I will command him. And Moshe and Yehoshua went, and stood in the Tent of Meeting.
And Havayah appeared in the Tent, in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood at the entrance of the Tent.

And Havayah said to Moshe: Behold, you shall lie with your fathers, and this people will rise, and stray after the foreign gods of the land that it is coming there, in its midst, and it will forsake Me, and break My covenant that I made with it.

And My anger will burn against them on that day, and I will forsake them, and hide My face from them, and they shall be devoured, and many evils and troubles shall find them, and they shall say on that day: Is it not because my Elokim is not in my midst that these evils have found me?
And I will surely hide My face on that day, because of all the evil that they did, for they turned to other gods.
And now, write for yourselves this song, and teach it to the children of Yisroel; put it in their mouths, so that this song shall be a witness for Me against the children of Yisroel.

For I will bring them to the land that I swore to their fathers, flowing with milk and honey, and they shall eat, and be satisfied, and grow fat, and turn to other gods, and serve them, and scorn Me, and break My covenant.

And it shall be, when many evils and troubles find them, this song shall testify before them as a witness, for it shall not be forgotten from the mouth of their seed, for I know their inclination, what they are doing today, before I bring them to the land that I swore.
And Moshe wrote this song on that day, and taught it to the children of Yisroel.
And He commanded Yehoshua son of Nun, and said: Be strong and of good courage, for you shall bring the children of Yisroel to the land that I swore to them, and I will be with you.
And it was, when Moshe finished writing the words of this Torah in a book, until they were complete.
And Moshe commanded the Leviim, who carry the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah, saying.
Take this book of the Torah, and place it beside the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah your Elokim, and it shall be there as a witness against you.
For I know your rebelliousness, and your stiff neck; behold, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against Havayah, and how much more after my death.
Gather to me all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, and I will speak these words in their ears, and call the heavens and the earth to witness against them.

For I know that after my death you will surely act corruptly, and turn aside from the way that I commanded you, and evil will befall you in the end of days, because you will do evil in the eyes of Havayah, to anger Him with the work of your hands.
And Moshe spoke in the ears of the whole assembly of Yisroel the words of this song, until they were complete.
Listen, heavens, and I will speak, and let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
My teaching shall drop as the rain, my speech shall flow as the dew, as showers upon grass, and as raindrops upon herbs.
For I will proclaim the name of Havayah; ascribe greatness to our Elokim.
The Rock — His work is perfect, for all His ways are justice; an El of faithfulness, and there is no wrong; righteous and upright is He.
They have corrupted themselves; their blemish is that they are not His children, a crooked and twisted generation.
Is this how you repay Havayah, O foolish and unwise people? Is He not your Father, who acquired you? He made you, and established you.
Remember the days of old; consider the years of generation after generation; ask your father, and he will tell you, your elders, and they will say to you.
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when He separated the sons of man, He set the borders of the peoples according to the number of the children of Yisroel.
For the portion of Havayah is His people; Yackov is the lot of His inheritance.
He found him in a wilderness land, and in a waste, a howling desert; He encircled him, He gave him understanding, He guarded him as the apple of His eye.
As an eagle stirs up its nest, hovers over its young, spreads its wings, takes them, carries them on its pinions.
Havayah alone led him, and no foreign god was with Him.
He set him upon the heights of the earth, and he ate the produce of the field, and He gave him honey to suck from the rock, and oil from the flinty stone.
Butter of cattle, and milk of sheep, with fat of lambs, and rams of Bashan, and goats, with fat of kidneys of wheat, and you drank the blood of the grape, foaming wine.
And Yeshurun grew fat and kicked; you grew fat, you grew thick, you grew gross, and he forsook Elokim, his Maker, and scorned the Rock of his salvation.
They angered Him with strangers; with abominations they provoked Him.
They sacrificed to demons, a non-god, gods that they did not know, new ones that came lately, which your fathers did not dread.
You forsook the Rock who bore you, and you forgot El, your Maker.
And Havayah saw, and scorned, because of the provocation of His sons and His daughters.
And He said: I will hide My face from them; I will see what their end is, for they are a generation of perversity, children in whom there is no faithfulness.
They provoked Me with a non-god; they angered Me with their vanities; and I will provoke them with a non-people; with a base nation I will anger them.
For a fire is kindled in My anger, and it burns to the lowest depths, and consumes the earth and its produce, and sets ablaze the foundations of the mountains.
I will heap evils upon them; I will spend My arrows upon them.
Wasted with hunger, and consumed with burning heat and bitter destruction, and I will send upon them the teeth of beasts, with the venom of creepers of the dust.
Outside the sword shall bereave, and inside terror shall bereave, both young man and virgin, suckling with the man of gray hair.
I said: I will scatter them to the corners; I will make their memory cease from among men.
Were it not that I feared the provocation of the enemy, lest their adversaries misunderstand, lest they say: Our hand is high, and Havayah did not do all this.
For they are a nation void of counsel, and there is no understanding in them.
If they were wise, they would understand this; they would discern their end.
How could one pursue a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them, and Havayah had delivered them up?
For their rock is not as our Rock, and our enemies are judges.
For their vine is of the vine of Sedom, and of the fields of Amorah; their grapes are grapes of poison, bitter clusters are theirs.
The venom of serpents is their wine, and the cruel poison of asps.
Is this not laid up with Me, sealed in My treasuries?
Vengeance is Mine, and recompense, at the time their foot slips, for the day of their calamity is near, and the things prepared for them hasten.
For Havayah will judge His people, and relent concerning His servants, when He sees that their power is gone, and none is left, bond or free.
And He will say: Where are their gods, the rock in which they sought refuge?
Who ate the fat of their sacrifices, drank the wine of their libations; let them rise and help you; let them be a shelter over you.
See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me; I kill and I make alive; I wound and I heal, and there is none who delivers from My hand.
For I lift My hand to the heavens, and say: As I live forever.
If I sharpen My flashing sword, and My hand takes hold of judgment, I will return vengeance to My enemies, and to those who hate Me I will repay.
I will make My arrows drunk with blood, and My sword shall devour flesh, from the blood of the slain and the captives, from the heads of the enemy leaders.
O nations, sing the praise of His people, for He will avenge the blood of His servants, and return vengeance to His adversaries, and atone for His land and His people.
And Moshe came and spoke all the words of this song in the ears of the people, he, and Hoshea son of Nun.
And Moshe finished speaking all these words to all Yisroel.
And he said to them: Set your hearts to all the words that I testify to you today, that you command them to your children, to take care to do all the words of this Torah.
For it is not an empty thing for you, for it is your life, and through this thing you shall prolong your days upon the land that you are crossing the Yarden to possess.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe on that very day, saying.
Go up to this mountain of Avarim, Mount Nevo, which is in the land of Moav, which faces Yericho, and see the land of Kena'an, which I am giving to the children of Yisroel as a possession.
And die on the mountain to which you ascend, and be gathered to your people, as Aharon your brother died on Mount Hor, and was gathered to his people.

Because you trespassed against Me in the midst of the children of Yisroel, at the waters of Merivah of Kadesh, in the wilderness of Tzin, because you did not sanctify Me in the midst of the children of Yisroel.
For from afar you shall see the land, but there you shall not come, to the land that I am giving to the children of Yisroel.
And this is the blessing with which Moshe, the man of Elokim, blessed the children of Yisroel before his death.
And he said: Havayah came from Sinai, and shone forth from Seir to them; He appeared from Mount Paran, and came with myriads of holiness; a fiery law came from His right hand, for them.
Indeed, He loves the peoples; all His holy ones are in Your hand, and they sat at Your feet, receiving Your words.
Moshe commanded us the Torah, a heritage of the congregation of Yackov.
And He became King in Yeshurun, when the heads of the people gathered, the tribes of Yisroel together.
Let Reuven live, and not die, and let his men be few.
And this is for Yehudah, and he said: Hear, Havayah, the voice of Yehudah, and bring him to his people; his hands shall fight for him, and You shall be a help against his adversaries.
And of Levi he said: Your Tumim and Your Urim are for Your pious one, whom You tested at Massah, with whom You contended at the waters of Merivah.
Who said of his father and of his mother: I have not seen him, and he did not know his brothers, and he did not know his children, for they kept Your word, and they guarded Your covenant.
They shall teach Your ordinances to Yackov, and Your Torah to Yisroel; they shall set incense before You, and whole offerings upon Your altar.
Bless, Havayah, his strength, and accept the work of his hands; crush the loins of those who rise against him, and his haters, so that they rise no more.
Of Binyamin he said: The beloved of Havayah shall dwell in safety by Him; He hovers over him all the day, and between his shoulders He dwells.
And of Yosef he said: His land is blessed of Havayah, with the bounty of heaven, with dew, and with the deep lying below.
And with the bounty of the crops of the sun, and with the bounty of the yield of the moons.
And from the tops of the ancient mountains, and from the bounty of the everlasting hills.

And from the bounty of the earth and its fullness, and the favor of Him who dwelled in the bush; let it come upon the head of Yosef, and upon the crown of the head of the one set apart from his brothers.

A firstborn bull is his glory, and his horns are the horns of the wild ox; with them he shall gore the peoples together, to the ends of the earth; and they are the myriads of Efrayim, and they are the thousands of Menasheh.
And of Zevulun he said: Rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out, and Yissachar, in your tents.
They shall call peoples to the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness, for they shall suck the abundance of the seas, and the hidden treasures of the sand.
And of Gad he said: Blessed is He who enlarges Gad; like a lion he dwells, and tears the arm, and the crown of the head.
And he saw the first part for himself, for there the portion of the lawgiver is hidden, and he came with the heads of the people; he did the righteousness of Havayah, and His judgments with Yisroel.
And of Dan he said: Dan is a lion's cub, leaping from Bashan.
And of Naftali he said: Naftali, satisfied with favor, and full of the blessing of Havayah, shall possess the sea and the south.
And of Asher he said: Asher is blessed above sons; let him be the favored of his brothers, and dip his foot in oil.
Iron and bronze shall be your bolts, and as your days, so shall your strength be.
There is none like El, O Yeshurun, who rides the heavens to your help, and in His majesty rules the skies.
The El of eternity is a dwelling, and underneath are the everlasting arms, and He drove the enemy out from before you, and said: Destroy.
And Yisroel dwells in safety, alone, the fountain of Yackov, in a land of grain and wine; His heavens drip dew.

Happy are you, Yisroel! Who is like you, a people saved by Havayah, the shield of your help, and the sword of your majesty? Your enemies shall cringe before you, and you shall tread upon their high places.
And Moshe went up from the plains of Moav to Mount Nevo, the top of the Pisgah, which faces Yericho, and Havayah showed him all the land, the Gilad, as far as Dan.
And all Naftali, and the land of Efrayim and Menasheh, and all the land of Yehudah, as far as the western sea.
And the south, and the plain, the valley of Yericho, the city of date palms, as far as Tzoar.

And Havayah said to him: This is the land that I swore to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yackov, saying: To your seed I will give it; I have shown it to you with your eyes, but there you shall not cross.
And Moshe, the servant of Havayah, died there, in the land of Moav, by the mouth of Havayah.
And He buried him in the valley, in the land of Moav, opposite Beit Peor, and no man knows his burial place to this day.
And Moshe was one hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eye had not dimmed, and his freshness had not departed.
And the children of Yisroel wept for Moshe in the plains of Moav thirty days, and the days of weeping of the mourning of Moshe were completed.
And Yehoshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, for Moshe had laid his hands upon him, and the children of Yisroel listened to him, and did as Havayah commanded Moshe.
And there has not risen a prophet again in Yisroel like Moshe, whom Havayah knew face to face.
For all the signs and the wonders that Havayah sent him to do in the land of Mitzrayim, to Paroh, and to all his servants, and to all his land.
And for all the mighty hand, and for all the great awe, that Moshe did before the eyes of all Yisroel.
